title: AI Architect
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
Serve as the principal architect for AI-enabled solutions supporting Finance, designing and delivering secure, scalable, and maintainable systems on AWS. Translate finance business needs into solution architectures that improve the quality, speed, and efficiency of financial planning, reporting, forecasting, and operations. Apply expertise in generative AI, agentic AI, machine learning, data architecture, cloud platforms, and software engineering to address significant business problems. Evaluate emerging technologies and integrate them where they provide measurable value, while ensuring solutions align with enterprise architecture, financial controls, data governance, security, and responsible-AI expectations. Act as a technical leader across Finance and IT, guiding architecture decisions and delivery teams from discovery through production and ongoing improvement.​
Responsibilities:
​​Lead architecture and solution design. Translate Finance requirements into end-to-end architectures for generative and agentic AI, machine learning, analytics, data, and software solutions on AWS, including integrations with enterprise platforms and existing finance systems.
​Identify and deliver high-value use cases. Partner with Finance stakeholders to assess opportunities such as forecasting, planning, reporting, reconciliation, close-process support, and document or transaction analysis; define solution scope, success measures, and implementation approaches.
​Design and implement secure AWS solutions. Select and apply appropriate AWS services and architectural patterns for data ingestion, storage, processing, analytics, AI/ML, application development, and deployment. Address scalability, resilience, performance, cost, and operational support.
​Establish data and AI governance. Ensure solutions use trusted, well-managed financial data, with appropriate lineage, quality controls, access management, retention, and auditability. Incorporate human review and escalation where warranted by the use case.
​Apply responsible-AI and model-lifecycle practices. Guide model and generative-AI evaluation, validation, monitoring, explainability, versioning, and change management in accordance with applicable enterprise standards and risk controls. Identify limitations and risks, including inaccurate outputs, bias, privacy exposure, and model drift.
​Protect financial information and controls. Incorporate security, privacy, segregation of duties, and applicable financial reporting and internal-control requirements into solution designs. Work with Finance, Security, Risk, Compliance, and other control partners to address requirements and support audits.
​Guide implementation and technical decisions. Evaluate build, reuse, and purchase options; recommend solutions based on business value, technical fit, risk, and total cost of ownership. Contribute to prototypes or code where needed to validate architecture and resolve key technical challenges.
​Advise stakeholders and delivery teams. Provide technical consultation to Finance and IT leaders, product owners, engineers, data teams, and operations partners. Communicate architectural choices, dependencies, risks, and trade-offs clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences.
​Promote reliable operations and continuous improvement. Define production-readiness expectations, including testing, deployment, monitoring, incident response, documentation, and ongoing cost and performance optimization. Incorporate user feedback and operational lessons into solution improvements.
​Provide technical leadership and uphold standards. Work autonomously with minimal direction, mentor architects and delivery team members as appropriate, and promote adherence to enterprise architecture, software-development, cloud, data, security, conduct, and other applicable corporate policies.
Bachelor’s Degree with 7 years of relevant experience; Master’s Degree with 6 years of experience; or PhD with 2 years of experience.
Respective years of experience in application development, solution architecture for AI applications.
​In-depth knowledge of the systems development life cycle, solution architecture, and the design and delivery of production-grade cloud, data, and analytics solutions for generative and agentic AI and ML applications.
​Demonstrated experience designing or implementing solutions on AWS, including appropriate services and patterns for data management, security, integration, deployment, monitoring, and cost optimization.
​Strong understanding of generative and agentic AI capabilities, limitations, and lifecycle practices, including evaluation, validation, monitoring, and responsible use.
​Knowledge of data governance, privacy, access control, auditability, and financial controls, with the ability to incorporate applicable requirements into solution designs.
​Proven track record of delivering creative technology solutions that advance business outcomes, with experience evaluating alternatives and balancing value, risk, feasibility, and total cost of ownership.
​Excellent written and oral English communication skills, including the ability to explain technical concepts, risks, and trade-offs to technical and nontechnical audiences.

description:

Purpose
We are seeking an Associate Director of AI & Automation Strategy to join the Finance Transformation team. The Associate Director will be responsible for supporting AI & Automation programs across the Finance organization with a specific focus on leading adoption and enablement efforts. You will lead the development of Proofs of Concept (“POCs”), including machine learning and forecasting solutions, and the scaling of initiatives across the organization. This role will also be responsible for supporting Finance strategy in alignment with AbbVie’s Enterprise vision.

Support the execution of the AI strategy in the Finance function.
Lead adoption efforts for Finance AI & Automation initiatives, including piloting solutions, collecting feedback, and ensuring successful rollout to end-users.
Lead and mentor a team of data scientists, providing technical guidance, setting priorities, and fostering best practices in model development.

Design and deliver ML training to build AI literacy and skills across Finance.
Help coordinate and drive communications and training to support data democratization and GenAI skill building within the Finance organization.
Assist with the creation and maintenance of a multi-year roadmap for Finance data and AI capabilities.
Collaborate closely with the Finance Transformation Data Strategy team and other business partners to rationalize data and support a central data architecture.
Support development, documentation, and adherence to governance frameworks as established by leadership.
Work with leaders and key stakeholders across Finance to identify, prioritize, and support delivery of data and AI-driven opportunities, managing expectations and communicating progress and impact.
Facilitate a culture of innovation, delivery, and measurable business impact through mentorship and promotion of best practices.
Build strong relationships across Finance, Business Technology Systems (BTS), and business unit teams to support coordination and adoption.
Ensure data is managed in compliance with regulations and company standards.
The ideal candidate will:
Execute the Finance Automation & AI strategy and influence decision-makers while leading data change management efforts across the Finance organization.
Bring hands-on ML and MLOps expertise to lead data science teams and turn models into adopted, scaled solutions.
Drive an effective data-driven culture that scales to meet the needs of all Finance functions across AbbVie.
Bachelor’s degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Data Science, Information Technology, or a related field.
Minimum 8+ years of progressive experience with exposure to data, AI, or automation programs; experience supporting or enabling data and AI initiatives preferred.
Experience building machine learning models and deploying them into production environments.
Hands-on experience with MLOps practices, including model deployment, monitoring, versioning, and lifecycle management.
Proven experience driving AI adoption, including piloting solutions, change management, user training, and scaling tools across an organization.
Familiarity with data strategy, architecture, and operations; proven success driving or supporting enterprise data initiatives as part of a larger program team.
Strong financial acumen and understanding of financial systems and processes.
Excellent collaboration, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
Ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders and drive adoption through training and enablement.
Experience supporting multiple concurrent projects in fast-paced, changing environments.
Demonstrated ability to work independently and as part of a cross-functional team.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with attention to detail and a focus on execution.

Purpose:
Oversees the direction, planning, execution and interpretation of clinical trials or research activities of a clinical development program. Participates in cross-functional teams to generate, deliver, and interpret high-quality clinical data supporting overall product scientific and business strategy.
Responsibilities:
Manages the design and implementation of one or more clinical development programs in support of an overall Product Development Plan, based on strong medical and scientific principles, knowledge of compliance and regulatory requirements, AbbVie’s customers, markets, business operations and emerging issues. Oversees project-related education of investigators, study site personnel and AbbVie study staff.
Has overall responsibility for oversight of clinical studies, monitoring overall study integrity and review, interpretation and communication of accumulating data pertaining to safety and efficacy of the molecule. Along with Clinical Operations, is responsible for oversight of study enrollment and overall timelines for key deliverables.
Responsible for design, analysis, interpretation, and reporting of scientific content of protocols, Investigator Brochures, Clinical Study Reports, regulatory submissions and responses and other program documents.
May oversee the work of Associate Scientific Directors and/or of Clinical Scientists working on the same or related programs.
Provides in-house clinical expertise for the molecule and disease, coordinating appropriate scientific activities with internal stakeholders as they relate to ongoing clinical projects. May participate in due diligence or other business development activity. As required by program needs, contributes in partnership with Discovery colleagues to design and implementation of translational strategies.
May serve on an Integrated Evidence Strategy Team (IEST), with responsibility for development of a rigorous, cross-functionally-aligned, vetted Clinical Development Plan with full consideration of contingencies and alternative approaches.
Acts as a clinical interface and actively solicits opinion leader interactions related to the molecule and disease area; partners with Medical Affairs, Commercial and other functions in these activities as required, consistent with corporate policies, to ensure that broad cross-functional perspectives are incorporated into Clinical Development Plans and protocols as appropriate.

Bachelors degree in the sciences; advanced degree (e.g., MS, PhD, PharmD) preferred.
Ability to provide input and direction to clinical research with appropriate supervision.
At least 5+ years of clinical trial experience in the pharmaceutical industry, academia, or equivalent.
Ability to oversee a clinical research program of moderate complexity with minimal supervision.
Ability to perform and bring out the best in others on a cross-functional global team.
Ability to interact externally and internally to support a global scientific and business strategy.
Knowledge of clinical trial methodology, regulatory and compliance requirements governing clinical trials and experience in development of clinical strategy and the design of study protocols.
Must possess excellent oral and written English communication skills.

This position leads, manages and coaches a regional team of Immunology Account Executives. Primary objectives include assessing regional business opportunity within assigned regional geography and priority Immunology Accounts (includes IDN Health Systems, Group Practices, hospital systems and specialty pharmacies) in order to deliver on assigned product performance goals.  It requires understanding of Immunology brand value propositions and implication for effective execution of these within target accounts, and with key customer influencers and decision-makers, by direct reports who engage key customers.  The position overlays multiple Immunology field sales organizations and AbbVie in-field support teams, requiring extensive communication and collaborative actions at the Region-level.
Responsibilities:
People Leadership

Lead KAM and internal business partnership communication and collaboration to insure highly effective, coordinated execution of AbbVie Immunology and IAE core priorities.  Monitor and enhance IFT partner clarity on IAE roles and priorities across key partner organizations.

Business Strategy (Analysis, Planning, Execution)
Clarify and integrate marketing strategies into regional execution, including sales training needs, during in-field and National/Regional meetings, with the purpose of elevating regional effectiveness within key account management.
Work with peers in Market Access and Trade to understand the changing Healthcare Landscape and proactively identify potential health system opportunities and conceptualize solutions using creativity and innovation within approved standards and resources.
Understand, execute and coach to appropriate use of approved promotional materials with health economic messaging.
Lead analysis and application of sales data in coordination direct reports, including coordination with partner sales management and sales operations, to inform business understanding and strategic planning and execution in order to achieve sales objectives.
Utilize IAE analytic tools, including CURO, to assess Regional and territory sales performance trends and create strategic selling initiatives to address performance opportunities.  Gather, organize and communicate monthly Regional performance vs. key business objectives.  Includes Q&I reports, CURO, Key Account Performance and resource execution.
Work with franchise leadership team to develop, implement and execute regional pull-through execution plans in support of IAE and Immunology core execution priorities (Business Planning, Selling Skills, Coaching).
Drive regional execution of business planning and Key Account planning process; manage direct reports to the same process.  This includes leading the effective assimilation of evolving account targeting and approved messaging strategies into regional execution.  Monitor account execution by direct reports using CURO and other business tools to insure accomplishment of execution expectations.
Engage prioritized accounts directly to establish relationships with key customers, in support of advancing organizational objectives.

Advanced analytical, coaching, direct people leadership, communication and presentation skills.
Knowledge of applicable regulations and standards affecting business.
Ability to examine complex business environment and develop/execute plans in response to market and account opportunities.
In-depth experience working within large accounts and across KAM/Matrix teams strongly preferred but not required.
Immunology sales/sales leadership preferred but not required.

description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
AbbVie’s Dermatology Franchise is seeking a strong analytical candidate to join a high-performing team supporting the new launches of RINVOQ in Vitiligo and Alopecia Areata. RINVOQ, AbbVie’s JAK inhibitor with a proven track record across multiple immunology indications, is now entering the market in these two serious dermatological conditions with significant unmet need. This is a unique opportunity to use analytics to drive early uptake, optimize investment, and accelerate growth across two new launches.
Major Responsibilities:
Analyze physician, patient, account, and competitive data at national and sub-national levels to track early launch performance, understand uptake and market dynamics in Vitiligo and Alopecia Areata, and identify opportunities and barriers to growth
Drive the launch learning agenda by analyzing patient journeys, new-to-brand and switch dynamics, treatment patterns, persistence, and competitive response across both new indications – translating findings into actionable insights and tactical adjustments
Develop fact-based promotional investment strategies and guide investment decisions through marketing mix and business optimization analyses to maximize performance and influence business growth across both new launches
Develop near-term launch KPIs and longer-term ROI measurements, and manage ongoing performance reporting, to inform recommendations that optimize personal and non-personal promotional channels
Support brand planning and financial forecasting by providing analytical inputs into the annual plan, long-range plan, and monthly estimates, ensuring assumptions are updated with actual launch performance; serve as a key conduit to Forecasting
Understand sub-national drivers of performance, including differences in dermatologist targeting and customer response across Vitiligo and Alopecia Areata, as well as cross-brand dynamics within the broader dermatology and RINVOQ portfolio, across distribution channels and customers
Leverage innovative, sophisticated analytic models that address critical issues while meeting key business criteria (e.g., cost, risk, business impact) and key technical criteria (e.g., reliability, validity, and predictability)
Lead fast-paced ad-hoc analytics projects, proactively identifying key business questions on product performance that inform strategic and tactical decision-making and the brand planning process, integrating multiple stakeholder perspectives
Effectively work with cross-functional partners to deliver integrated analytics that reflect the diverse contributions across functions
Lead contract support and external suppliers to enhance the use of advanced modeling and analytic methods and fully leverage available data assets to produce actionable results
Bachelor’s Degree required, with a concentration in marketing/sales/quantitative analysis preferred.  Advanced degree preferred.
7+ years of relevant experience in quantitative analysis of sales and marketing information is required, including use of this information in the development of business plans and strategies.  Experience within the Pharma/Biotech industry is a plus.
Strong analytical reasoning abilities, intellectual curiosity, strong business acumen, and creativity in problem solving. Experience with current methods Analytics/Machine Learning.
Advanced experience with 3rd party pharmaceutical data sources like IQVIA/SHS Sales Data (APLD, DDD, Xponent, NSP, NPA), and Specialty pharmacy data and one or multiple analytic domains (promo optimization, digital, launch support, etc) is a plus
Deep hands-on expertise in current analytical methods & tools (including machine learning)
Advanced communication and influencing skills
Advanced agility, project management and prioritization skills
Advanced vendor management skills
Proven ability to collaborate effectively and to influence in a matrixed organization
High motivation, strong work-ethic and positive attitude while working under tight timelines

4-5 years of medical/scientific publications (or related) experience required. Pharmaceutical industry or related (eg, medical communication agency) experience required
Demonstrated abilities in a leadership capacity required
Ability to understand and interpret medical data require
Knowledge of product therapeutic area preferred; working knowledge of statistical concepts and techniques required
Knowledge of clinical/scientific publication structure, content, and quality. Knowledge of scientific publication regulations and best practices
Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal, with demonstrated success in creating and delivering effective presentations to senior-level audiences

We are searching for a highly motivated Senior Scientist I to join our Analytical Development team at Waltham, MA. Our team is responsible for the development, qualification, and execution of analytical methods to provide product and process understanding for biological entities from discovery through commercial stages. As a Senior Scientist I, you will be a part of the Analytical Characterization Group (ACG) within the Analytical Development department. ACG focuses on providing routine, investigative, and in-depth characterization as well as proteomics analyses of AbbVie's biologics to support product and process development for early-phase, late-phase, and commercial programs using liquid chromatography mass spectrometry (LC-MS), spectroscopy, and various other biophysical characterization assays. The successful candidate will contribute to the development and performance of analytical assays and will contribute to the continuous improvement and innovation within ACG and the Analytical Development department. The incumbent operates with a high degree of independence, contributes project science in their area of expertise, and develops productive collaborations across disciplines.
Responsibilities:
Independently perform LC-MS analyses (e.g., intact, reduced, sub-unit, peptide mapping, and disulfide bond mapping) of AbbVie's biologics to provide sequence verification, post-translational modification profiles, sequence variant levels, and disulfide bond profiles.
Independently perform separation methods (e.g., fractionation of variants) and biophysical methods of AbbVie's biologics to support characterization studies.
Design and execute experiments for method development and/or investigations.
Generate and communicate precise, reliable, and reproducible data in a timely manner.
Organize and document experiments and results in an electronic laboratory notebook; author and review protocols, method development reports, and technical characterization reports.
Represent the Analytical Development department in cross-functional program teams as characterization lead for AbbVie's biologics in development pipeline.
Maintain laboratory equipment, provide troubleshooting, and coordinate services/PMs.
Routinely demonstrate scientific initiative and creativity in research or development activities.
Highly autonomous and productive in performing laboratory research or method development, requiring only minimal direction from or interaction with supervisor.
Direct mentorship of junior scientists and others in the lab.
PhD or Masters in chemistry, biology, biochemistry or related technical discipline with typically 0–3 (PhD) or 8+ (MS) years of relevant experience in a biotech/pharmaceutical industry setting.
Preferred Qualifications:
Hands-on experience with protein mass spectrometry, liquid chromatography, capillary electrophoresis and protein biophysical characterization
Strong fundamental understanding of protein structure, post-translational modifications, and analytical methods used for protein characterization.
Experience with bioinformatics tools to process and analyze mass spectrometry data.
Proficient with Windows 10 and Microsoft Office (Outlook, Excel, Word, and PowerPoint).
Excellent written communication, oral communication, organization, and multitasking skills.
Hardworking and motivated to drive both efficiency and quality in a fast-paced and collaborative environment.
Understand and adhere to corporate standards regarding code of conduct, safety, and appropriate handling of materials.

description:
Join Adobe’s Experience Manager (AEM) Customer Engineering team—the expert group at the front lines of helping enterprises craft, deliver and optimize digital experiences at scale. Our team supports AEM developers and business users across the globe, guiding them through performance tuning, problem solving, debugging complex issues and expanding what’s possible with AEM as a Cloud Service.

location: San Jose; San Francisco; Seattle; New York
description:
The Opportunity
Adobe’s Business Ethics & Integrity organization is continuing to evolve our data-driven, risk-based approach to compliance - one that proactively identifies emerging risks, continuously evaluates the effectiveness of our controls, and uses data and technology to generate meaningful insights and drive continuous improvement.
We’re looking for a Compliance Risk & Assurance professional to help continue maturing these capabilities across Adobe’s global Business Ethics & Integrity program. This role will connect compliance risk assessments, monitoring, targeted compliance reviews, and analytics to help us understand where our most significant risks are, whether our compliance processes and controls are effectively mitigating those risks, and where we should focus our efforts and resources.
You’ll work across Business Ethics & Integrity and partner closely with Legal, Internal Audit, and other teams to develop scalable, risk-based assurance and monitoring capabilities. You’ll also support compliance due diligence in M&A and explore opportunities to leverage data, analytics, automation, and emerging technologies - including AI - to strengthen risk identification, improve efficiency, and generate actionable insights.
This is an opportunity to help shape how a global technology company identifies and manages compliance risks, evaluates program effectiveness, and drives continuous improvement.
What You'll Do
Develop and execute compliance risk assessments to identify, evaluate, and prioritize ethics and compliance risks across Adobe’s businesses, geographies, and operations.
Design and implement risk-based compliance monitoring and assurance activities to evaluate the effectiveness of compliance processes and controls, identify gaps, and drive remediation and continuous improvement.
Build and enhance continuous monitoring capabilities, leveraging compliance and business data to identify emerging risks, trends, anomalies, and potential control weaknesses across key compliance risk areas.
Develop meaningful risk indicators, dashboards, metrics, and reporting to provide leadership with actionable insights into compliance risks, program effectiveness, and opportunities for improvement.
Partner with Legal, Internal Audit, and business stakeholders to evaluate findings, identify root causes, develop practical remediation plans, and strengthen compliance processes and controls.
Support M&A compliance risk assessments and due diligence, including identifying potential ethics and compliance risks and supporting post-close integration and remediation.
Leverage analytics, automation, AI, and emerging technologies to improve the efficiency, scalability, and effectiveness of compliance risk assessment, monitoring, and assurance activities.

8+ years of relevant experience in corporate ethics and compliance, compliance risk management, or compliance monitoring and assurance, ideally within a global company or similarly complex environment. Strong understanding of corporate ethics and compliance programs, including key compliance risk areas, regulatory expectations, risk assessment methodologies, compliance monitoring, and approaches to evaluating program effectiveness.
Demonstrated experience designing, implementing, or executing compliance risk assessments, risk-based compliance monitoring, targeted compliance reviews, or compliance assurance activities.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
The Opportunity
Adobe Workfront is the work management platform that enterprises rely on to plan, run, and measure work across thousands of people, projects, and approvals. Behind it are engineering teams who understand both the platform and the complex, often regulated environments where customers use it.
The Forward Deployed Engineer role sits at the intersection of software engineering, solution architecture, and technical consulting. You will be embedded with Workfront's most strategic customers, working directly with their teams to solve hard platform challenges, design scalable integrations, and build what is needed to unblock adoption and expansion.
You will work in a cross-functional Customer Pod: a small, autonomous team with end-to-end ownership. As a senior engineer, you set technical direction for your accounts, mentor other builders, and close the gap between what customers need and what the platform delivers.
What You'll Do
Partner with strategic customers to understand their workflows, systems, security requirements, and business goals.
Turn complex customer problems into scalable solution designs, reference architectures, and working prototypes.
Build and ship custom integrations and extensions across Workfront Workflow, Workfront Planning, Workfront Fusion, APIs, and adjacent Adobe and third-party systems.
Investigate and resolve production issues, from data and permissions models to automation, reporting, and performance.
Lead architecture workshops, health checks, and technical deep dives that earn customer trust.
Prototype and iterate quickly, using AI-assisted tools as a standard part of how you work.
Feed field patterns back to product and engineering to shape the Workfront roadmap.
Mentor engineers in the pod and set practices for how the team documents decisions and learnings.
Own the technical relationship with assigned accounts from discovery through go-live and expansion.
What Success Looks Like
We hire for demonstrated impact, not credential accumulation. Strong candidates show:
Customer empathy. You meet customers on their terms and understand their constraints and definition of success.
Ownership at senior level. You find problems before they are assigned and drive them to resolution without waiting for permission.
Clear communication. You explain complex ideas to technical and executive audiences in workshops, architecture reviews, and briefings.
Business acumen. You understand the use case before choosing the technology.
Software craft. You write code, build prototypes, and ship working software. Your designs reflect implementation reality.
Data and integration judgment. You weigh trade-offs in data models, API design, and system integration.
Growth mindset and AI fluency. You use AI-assisted development tools (Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, or equivalent) to design, prototype, and deliver, and you build toward agentic capabilities.
Typical background: 8 to 12 years in software engineering, solution architecture, technical consulting, or customer-facing engineering. What matters is what that experience produced, not the title or the number of years.
Your Domain

title: Regional Workplace Operations Manager
description:

Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join:
The Regional Workplace Operations Manager sits at the intersection of workplace experience, events, and gathering & culture. This role is responsible for bringing our brand to life by creating an intentional, welcoming, and high-functioning office experience that enables employees, leaders, and guests to feel connected, productive, and inspired. Just like our hosts can offer differentiated experiences to our guests, our Regional Workplace Operations Manager exemplifies those aspirational expectations.
This role serves as the connective tissue across office operations, hospitality, employee engagement, and local community experience. They partner closely with cross-functional stakeholders including Talent, IT, Security, Communications, Executive Support, and local leaders to ensure each office reflects Airbnb’s culture and values in a meaningful and scalable way. They integrate platform hosts in the day to day office experience spotlighting service and experience hosts as appropriate.
The Difference You Will Make:
As the Regional Workplace Operations Manager, you are the primary steward of the employee and guest experience within your office. You create a hospitality-forward environment where people feel welcomed, supported, and connected to Airbnb and each other.
You will oversee the daily office experience while also leading local gathering and engagement efforts that strengthen culture and community. You will direct and coordinate embedded vendors and operational partners to ensure seamless execution across hospitality, food, facilities, and events. You will provide oversight and mentorship to Office Managers within your region, ensuring consistency of standards and experience across proximate offices.
Success in this role requires strong operational ownership, exceptional interpersonal instincts, creativity, and the ability to navigate ambiguity while balancing both strategic thinking and hands-on execution.
You must have your finger on the pulse and anticipate the needs of each guest.

Lead Through Hospitality
Maintain a visible, approachable, and highly responsive presence within the office community.
Create a warm, thoughtful, and highly responsive environment where employees and visitors feel genuinely welcomed and cared for.
Lead with calmness, flexibility, and attention to detail while balancing multiple priorities and adapting to changing business needs.
Support and guide vendors and partners to operate as one cohesive hospitality team in service of the office community.
Drive Operational Excellence
Establish and maintain office operating standards that ensure consistency of hospitality, communication, service delivery, and workplace experience.
Monitor office utilization, employee feedback, operational performance, and service quality to identify opportunities for improvement.
Contribute local insights and best practices that help shape the evolution of workplace standards across the broader portfolio.
Develop repeatable processes and playbooks that enable scalable, high-quality office experiences.
Own the Office Experience
Oversee the holistic daily office experience, ensuring the space operates smoothly and delivers a welcoming, hospitality-forward environment for employees and guests.
You have a strong sense of ownership. Treat the office as your listing.

Provide operational oversight and direction to on-site vendors and service partners.

Act as the “Voice of the Office,” helping employees navigate the workplace experience and ensuring the office feels connected, informed, and supported.
Monitor employee sentiment and proactively identify opportunities to improve the office experience, communication, and engagement.

Ensure the office is consistently prepared to support high-visibility visits, events, and business moments.
Partner with Regional Gathering Programs to support successful delivery of offsites, leadership visits and strategic gatherings.
Provide local stakeholder coordination, hospitality leadership, vendor management, and onsite execution support as needed.
Support onsite execution for local events, offsites, and engagement activities, ensuring thoughtful hospitality, operational excellence, and strong attendee experience.
Adapt office experiences to local needs while maintaining consistency with Airbnb culture and values.

Develop strong relationships with local leaders, executive admins, Airfinity groups, cross-functional partners and other key stakeholders.
Act as a trusted partner and connector across teams, helping identify opportunities to strengthen office culture, engagement, and employee experience.
Partner with leaders to support meaningful moments of connection within the office and across teams.

title: Air Program Manager, AWS Environmental
description:
Join a diverse, dynamic, and enthusiastic team of environmental compliance professionals who play a leading role in air quality permitting and compliance at Amazon Web Services (AWS), where we have a history of leading the world in innovative technologies and services. As a member of the Environmental team, you will support environmental programs aimed at ensuring compliance with air quality regulations and standards in the Americas while also enabling AWS's growth around the world.
As an Air Program Manager, your primary focus will be serving as the air compliance subject matter expert (SME) across an Americas sub-region, providing programmatic oversight and ensuring alignment of compliance practices across all AWS data centers. You will build regional-level compliance infrastructure (frameworks, standards, tools, and visibility) and provide functional direction to the Regional Environmental Engineers (REEs) who execute compliance at their sites. You will work closely with the Environmental team, engineering, operations teams, vendors, and other partners to ensure consistent application of air quality compliance programs, particularly those related to Tier 4 compliant diesel generators. Your role will involve providing technical expertise on local, state, and federal air regulations and creating strategies for continuous improvement in air compliance management. As the team's air compliance SME, you will support REEs across the region to resolve complex air compliance challenges and drive environmental performance. You will also play a key role in standardizing incident response and reporting protocols related to air compliance events.
The successful candidate will have extensive knowledge of air compliance and regulatory requirements in North America, demonstrated ability to develop and standardize complex compliance systems across multiple jurisdictions, and proven experience leading air quality initiatives that drive environmental performance and sustainability. The ideal candidate will excel at providing strategic guidance while maintaining strong attention to technical details and have a track record of successfully collaborating with diverse stakeholders to implement environmental compliance programs at scale.
Key job responsibilities
- Build and lead regional air quality compliance programs, providing standards and functional direction to in-region engineers across North and South America
- Set and maintain the regional framework for compliance with federal, state, and local air quality regulations related to emergency backup power systems
- Ensure compliance with EPA regulations including 40 CFR 60 Subpart IIII (Standards of Performance for Stationary Compression Ignition Internal Combustion Engines)
- Develop and implement air quality monitoring programs and compliance tracking systems for permitted backup power generation (Tier 2/Tier 4 diesel generators, natural gas, etc)
- Establish standardized emissions testing programs and protocols that engineers and testing firms execute at their sites
- Provide technical guidance on air quality compliance requirements
- Support emergency response planning related to air quality incidents
- Collaborate with the air permitting team and in-region engineers to ensure operational compliance with existing permit conditions
- Stay current with evolving air quality regulations and industry best practices for diesel generator management
- Develop and deliver air quality compliance training for relevant staff
- Establish and track key performance indicators (KPIs) for air quality compliance
About the team
AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS) owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain, and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.
Basic qualifications: - 5+ years of increasing responsibilities in EHS or environmental programs in manufacturing, production, or service operations experience, or Bachelor's degree
- 5+ years with air permitting and/or compliance experience at local, state, federal levels
Preferred qualifications: - Experience managing multiple projects and priorities across teams in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment
- Experience that includes strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and effective communication abilities
- Experience developing and implementing environmental compliance programs including regulated waste, water, and air regulations in accordance with applicable laws
- 3+ years with engine specific regulations including 40 CFR 63 Subpart ZZZZ and 40 CFR 60 Subpart IIII

Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. title: Senior Human Rights Due Diligence Advisor, WW Sustainability
description:
Join us at the forefront of Amazon's sustainability initiatives to work on environmental and social advancements that support Amazon's long-term worldwide sustainability strategy. At Amazon, we're working to be the most customer-centric company on earth. To get there, we need exceptionally talented, bright, and driven people who are passionate about making a meaningful impact on communities and the environment while helping shape the future of sustainable business practices.
The Worldwide Sustainability (WWS) organization capitalizes on Amazon's scale and speed to build a more resilient and sustainable company. We manage our social and environmental impacts globally and drive solutions that enable our customers, businesses, and the world to become more sustainable. Through innovative programs and strategic partnerships, we're creating lasting positive change in the communities where we operate while advancing Amazon's commitment to environmental stewardship and social responsibility.
Amazon's Human Rights & Social Impact program drives customer trust, business continuity, and sustainable social impact by embedding respect for human rights throughout Amazon’s entire value chain. We implement company-wide standards and commitments such as our Global Human Rights Principles (GHRP) and Supply Chain Standards (SCS) . We seek to continuously improve the tools and processes used in integrating human rights due diligence across the business. We work with businesses across Amazon to embed and scale respect for human rights. Within HRSI, the Human Rights Due Diligence (HRDD) team works with businesses to identify and prioritize human rights risks across the value chain, and develops the methodologies that assess those risks and measure the performance of business efforts to prevent and mitigate harm.
We are hiring a Senior Human Rights Due Diligence Advisor to serve as a specialized subject matter expert operating at the intersection of two areas: (1) due diligence advisory services and (2) methodology and tool development. This is a senior individual-contributor role for someone who can work both strategically and tactically, operate with limited guidance in ambiguous problem spaces, and act as the primary point of accountability for complex human rights due diligence work.
As a trusted advisor to HRSI teams, Worldwide Sustainability partners, and business customers, you will own multiple or complex business relationships, conduct end-to-end risk analyses, and translate international human rights standards into operational guidance. Critically, you will not only bring deep knowledge of frameworks such as the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights; you will operationalize them by designing quantitative, data-driven methodologies and risk scoring logics that make human rights risk measurable and comparable at enterprise scale. You will also serve as a single-threaded leader for methodology and tool development, defining the strategy and frameworks that enable the entire team's success.
Key job responsibilities
- Own multiple or complex business relationships for human rights due diligence, serving as the primary point of accountability for assigned businesses.
- Work with businesses to identify and prioritize human rights risks across the value chain.
- Conduct end-to-end risk analyses, write comprehensive risk reports, and translate findings into actionable insights for business stakeholders.
- Design and develop quantitative, data-driven methodologies and risk scoring logics that assess human rights risk and measure the performance of business efforts to prevent and mitigate harm.
- Act as a single-threaded leader (STL) for the end-to-end development of enterprise due diligence methodologies and tools, often in ambiguous contexts where the desired outcome is not previously defined.
- Partner with other HRDD advisors to understand their use cases and needs, defining strategy and frameworks that enable the broader team to succeed.
- Assess risks across differing business models, supply chain structures, and regulatory environments while maintaining a big-picture view of how human rights risks connect to business goals and compliance requirements.
- Serve as a trusted advisor to HRSI teams and Amazon businesses, translating international standards into operational realities.

- - 8+ years of experience in human rights, sustainability, ESG, responsible sourcing, or corporate due diligence.

- - Experience developing quantitative, data-driven risk methodologies or scoring logics that translate qualitative standards into measurable, comparable outputs.
- - Familiarity with human rights due diligence regulation (e.g., CSDDD, CSRD, national supply chain due diligence and modern slavery laws).
- - Experience conducting human rights or value chain risk assessments and translating findings into actionable recommendations for business stakeholders.
- - Pragmatic operator who thrives in a fast-paced environment, working across functions and business teams with competing priorities to find actionable, high-judgment solutions. - Partner with internal customers to define ambiguous problem statements and translate them into clear technical requirements and specifications
- Contribute to Amazon's MHE sourcing and integration strategy by evaluating vendor capabilities, performing technical assessments, and generating data-driven recommendations

Global Engineering Services (GES) North America (NA) Technical Vendor Management operates at the intersection of engineering execution and vendor partnership across North America. title: Hardware Systems Engineering Manager
description:
Apple is where you do the best work of your life. Behind every Apple product is a remarkable collaboration of engineering disciplines, where innovation, precision, and attention to detail shape experiences enjoyed by millions of people worldwide.
Imagine shaping how the next generation of Apple products is designed, understood, and continuously improved. From silicon to complete systems, the ability to observe, measure, and understand hardware behavior is fundamental to building exceptional products.
Our team works at the intersection of product architecture, electrical engineering, and intelligent metrology, partnering with design teams to develop innovative electrical architectures, embedded observability, and scalable measurement solutions. We influence product designs early, enabling deeper system insights through hardware, firmware, and software integration. Where additional capabilities are needed, we architect specialized instrumentation and measurement platforms that extend our understanding of product behavior from early development through production.
We are looking for an engineering leader who combines deep technical expertise, strategic thinking, and a passion for developing exceptional teams. 3+ years of engineering management experience with strong hands-on hardware systems expertise, or 7+ years of technical leadership experience with demonstrated readiness for people management.
Extensive experience in hardware systems development, including architecture, schematic design, PCB layout, bring-up, characterization, and deployment.
Strong electrical engineering fundamentals spanning analog, power electronics, mixed-signal, and high-speed digital design.
Demonstrated ability to lead complex engineering initiatives and collaborate across multiple technical disciplines.

Experience developing scalable engineering platforms and reusable hardware architectures across multiple products.

title: InfoSec Development Program (ISDP), Full-Time Opportunities
description:
The Apple Information Security (AIS) team is responsible for developing services to find and mitigate security risks faced by Apple. • Manage and improve critical security infrastructure services for authentication, logging, security monitoring, and detection
• Provide security assurance across the entirety of Apple via penetration testing, adversary simulation, threat modeling, and security automation
• Lead ground breaking security efforts at a scale you’ll only be able to find at Apple
• Work multi-functionally with teams throughout Apple on technology and initiatives to improve security and bring security standard methodologies to our products and services
• Develop production infrastructure fixes to complex vulnerabilities and design architectures to minimize business risks
Minimum qualifications: Undergraduate or graduate degree in CS, CE, ECE, EECS, IS, IT, or other related fields of study.
Related software engineering internship or job experience
Strong software design, problem solving and debugging skills
Experience with one or more programming languages such as C/C++, JavaScript, Go and Python
Passion for high-quality code, tests, CI/CD, documentation, and production services
Act with high ethical standards and integrity
Preferred qualifications: Excellent interpersonal skills, and the capability of working with cross functional technical and business teams and varying levels of management
Passionate about information security and keeping Apple’s customers safe

title: ML Agent Engineer
description:

description:

title: Machine Learning Engineer, Computer Vision
description:

title: Physical Design Methodology CAD Engineer
description:

title: Physical Failure Analysis Engineer
description:
In this role, you will deliver professional failure analysis and characterization solutions across a wide array of next-generation materials, silicon devices, and advanced products; and collaborate with multi-functional teams to launch the world's most premiere products.

You will provide samples optimized for high-resolution imaging, micro-probing, and nano-probing, conveying analytical findings to engineering teams and upper management. Deep understanding of fundamental failure analysis methodologies, defect isolation workflows, and sample preparation principles
Extensive hands-on experience with mechanical cross-sectioning, encapsulation, and iterative planar polishing
Extensive hands-on experience with CNC-based polishers, decapsulation, parallel lapping of MLBs, and packaged die
Hands-on proficiency with wet and dry etch methods for sample de-processing and material removal
Proficiency in optical microscopy and basic understanding of mechanical and microelectronic assemblies
Strong 3D spatial awareness and ability to visualize and reconstruct internal device architectures in three dimensions
Proven track record of independently troubleshooting preparation challenges, prioritizing tasks, and completing projects under tight deadlines
Strong technical writing, reporting, and verbal communication skills in English
Ability to work collaboratively and effectively across multidisciplinary engineering organizations
Excellent communication skills

title: Technical Program Manager and Manufacturing Quality Engineer
description:
Imagine what you could do here. At Apple, new ideas have a way of becoming extraordinary products, services, and customer experiences very quickly. Bring passion and dedication to your job and there's no telling what you could accomplish. The people here at Apple don’t just create products — they create the kind of wonder that’s revolutionized entire industries. It’s the diversity of those people and their ideas that inspires the innovation that runs through everything we do, from amazing technology to industry-leading environmental efforts. Join Apple, and help us leave the world better than we found it.
In this highly visible role, you will have process (TPM) and quality engineering (MQE) responsibility for next generation Apple products. This will require you to lead selection, implementation & optimization of manufacturing processes and quality planning and deployment.
In the TPM responsibility, you will utilize your Engineering experience and work cross functionally with Product Design Engineering and Industrial Design to assess product features for manufacturability, and recommend capable processes and equipment.
In the MQE responsibility, you work in tandem with Apple's renowned designers to develop measurement & metrology technologies, quality control plans, information systems, and manufacturing methods that achieve industry-leading specifications at massive production scale. We handle a network of supplier factories worldwide, with responsibility for our partners to deliver to bold schedules. Our focus is on elegant execution of extraordinary industrial designs, resulting in products that thrill our customers.
Process Development:
Planning, proposing, and leading experiments to produce timely and accurate analyses used to drive design, development, and supply chain decisions.
Assessing the suitability of a fabrication technology for a given part design. Planning validation exercises to demonstrate initial feasibility as well as manufacturing capability. Analyzing results of validation exercises and provide technical recommendations.
Reviewing progress of development activities at supplier locations and serve as point of escalation for critical process related issues.
New Product Introduction:
Help to drive process development and capability assessment activities, reviewing part design documentation to ensure alignment with process capability.
Assigns specific tasks and work with Apple suppliers to support process development and/or data gathering activities. Set clear goals for results and provide timely reviews of performance throughout program.
Establish validation procedures to figure out acceptance of tooling into development builds as well as mass production.
Supplier Execution:
Review supplier tool design, process flow, equipment selection, DFM, and DOE proposals. Identify shortfalls and corrective actions to ensure design compliance.
Work with supplier engineering teams to map out process development exercises, secure resources, and commit to schedules in line with program goals
Assess supplier readiness to support build events and production ramp. Identify potential execution issues and provide recommendations to mitigate risk.
You will utilize your Quality Engineering background in the following areas:
Quality Planning
Apply solid understanding of quality control and manufacturing concepts to develop specific Product Quality Plan (PQP) appropriate to program and commodity.
Coordinate all Quality Engineering functions for a program, serving as project manager to lead efforts at supplier locations.
Actively participate in the program planning and monitoring process assuming responsibility for key deliverables at all milestones.
Provide technical direction and guidance to other Quality Engineers supporting the implementation of the PQP.
Assess measurability and creatively address concerns directly with stakeholders. Identify and direct studies to implement improvements in measuring method where appropriate.
Establish audit procedures appropriate to program and supplier to ensure adherence to Apple quality standards. Implement FAI and Cp/Cpk reviews of mechanical parts.
Supplier Quality Management
Assists supplier selection process for new products and second sourcing activities supporting qualification/disqualification decisions.
Review PQP with supplier and other Apple functional groups to optimize supplier quality programs. Evaluates supplier readiness and adherence to PQP at all development and qualification stages.
Monitor each supplier's performance through measurement of production line statistics, company inspections, and audits. Prepare summary of performance and communicate to appropriate management to ensure effective corrective action plans can be promptly executed.
At Apple, a Supplier Quality Engineer defines product cosmetic specifications and manufacturing quality control methods. Reviews processing techniques and methods applied in the manufacture, fabrication, and evaluation of products. Involvement may begin at any step from product concept to full-scale manufacturing. Coordinates design requirement review with appropriate engineering/scientific personnel to ensure capability of manufacturing processes. Compiles and evaluates data to determine appropriate limits and variables for process, material, and part specifications. May conceive and plan projects involving definition and selection of new concepts, product inspection technology, and approaches in the processing or development of new or improved processes. Recommends and implements equipment and process modifications to improve production efficiencies, manufacturing techniques and production yields for existing products. Develops and conducts statistical analysis such as Design of Experiments (DOE) and Statistical Process Control (SPC) targeting cause of failure for yield loss and improving quality.
Minimum qualifications: BS in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Engineering Management.
1+ years experience supporting new product launches from a mechanical, process engineering, quality planning, quality engineering or product development perspective.
Experience developing process quality plans, supplier quality audits, and driving corrective actions and failure analysis efforts.
Knowledge of mechanical quality and reliability concepts, supplier management, and general manufacturing operations.
Requires International travel to supplier sites.
Preferred qualifications: Experience with soft materials (non-wovens, wovens, knits, leather) and inputs to those materials (yarns, raw materials) is strongly preferred. Experience with mechanical fabricated parts, or adhesives, glues, jigs, fixtures, tooling, injection molding, plastics experience may be acceptable.
International experience, particularly in Asia is a plus
Must have proven hands-on mechanical ability. Demonstrate excellent written and verbal communication skills. Domestic and International travel required. Experience with highly cosmetic parts a plus.

Demonstrate Apple’s values of inclusion and diversity in daily activities.
Minimum qualifications: You should:
Be available to work a schedule based on business needs that may include nights, weekends, and public holidays in the retail store, and reliably attend work as scheduled, in line with local laws and subject to any approved accommodations.
Have experience in retail or sales, or related work experience.
Possess the visual inspection and fine motor skills to safely perform hardware repairs.
Have experience troubleshooting hardware and software issues in a customer service environment.
Preferred qualifications: You can:
Demonstrate technical expertise of Apple products and services, including repairing devices.
Analyze problems and follow troubleshooting steps to identify the root cause of a technical issue.
Navigate customer service issues with care and strong interpersonal skills.

title: Wi-Fi / Bluetooth Software System Performance Engineer, Wireless Technologies & Ecosystems
description:
Join the Wireless Technologies and Ecosystems organization and be part of an outstanding team of engineers driving innovation on products used by millions worldwide! Our team is looking for a highly motivated Performance Engineer to drive optimization of software design for Apple’s latest products, including the next generation of iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, AirPods, and Mac!
Be a key member of the Connectivity Firmware Performance team, where you'll work on software design testing and optimization from early prototypes until productization. The work involves devising performance evaluation methodologies on SW/HW prototypes, analyzing logs, and making recommendations for implementing software design based on trade-off analysis at a system & product level.
Minimum qualifications: You have a background or research experience in RF, Digital, and Wireless communications
Programming experience in C or C++

The Continuous Control Monitoring (CCM) team, part of Enterprise Risk & Security, builds and operates DASH, Cox Automotive’s compliance monitoring platform. DASH brings together security and infrastructure data from CrowdStrike, Wiz, Qualys, Akamai, AWS, ServiceNow, GitHub, and other enterprise sources. We’re looking for an engineer who is equally comfortable building data pipelines and building the applications people use to interact with that data. You’ll help extend DASH in two directions. Cox Fleet is currently hiring a  Mobile Diesel Technician Level 2 or Sr Mobile Diesel Mechanic (Level 3)
The Mobile Diesel Technician Level II will be responsible for performing licensed DOT inspections, Preventative Maintenance inspections, light and follow-up repairs, light mechanical/hydraulic/electrical and electronic diagnostics, and other duties as assigned.  The Mobile Diesel Technician II can perform more advanced diagnostics and repairs under the supervision of a Sr Mobile Diesel Technician or higher. The Diesel Technician II continues to learn additional advanced mechanical skills and diagnostic techniques.  A successful Diesel Technician II complies with all company policies and achieves high level performance metrics.
DUTIES:
Perform scheduled preventative maintenance (“PM”), DOT Inspections and follow up repairs on light, medium and heavy-duty vehicles in a mobile/field environment.
Perform minor adjustment and repairs on various types of truck equipment including, but not limited to the following: Electrical/Brake/Cooling Systems, Starters/Alternators, Fan clutches, Engine electronics, Diesel steering systems, Engines (gas and diesel), Transmissions (manual and automatic), Clutches, Differentials, etc.
Diagnose, adjust, and repair various types of truck equipment including, but not limited to the following: Electrical/Brake/Cooling Systems, Starters/Alternators, Air conditioning systems, Fan clutches, Engine electronics, Diesel steering systems, Engines (gas and diesel), Transmissions (manual and automatic), Clutches, Differentials, etc.
Inspect, test, and listen to defective equipment to diagnose malfunctions, using test instruments such as handheld computers and pressure gauges.

As an Associate Manager on the DoorDash for Business Catering team, you will own the Dasher and delivery experience for catering—making sure large, high-stakes catering orders show up on time, get handed off and set up correctly, and reach the customer the way they expect.

DoorDash Labs builds autonomous delivery robots and other autonomy solutions for DoorDash’s delivery platform. Operational Intelligence is a technical team within our Technical Operations organization, developing the internal applications, data integrations, and AI-powered workflows that help our robotics fleet operate reliably and efficiently. We work directly with fleet support, service, Engineering, and Product teams to turn operational challenges into practical technical solutions. Our work makes information more accessible, improves troubleshooting and decision-making, and reduces the manual effort required to support a growing fleet. Being embedded within Operations means we stay close to the people using our tools and see the impact of what we build.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role within Technical Operations, with software development as a core responsibility. We are looking for someone who brings strong systems experience: understanding how frontend and backend services fit together, how APIs connect them, and how software is built, deployed, and operated in production.You will own defined features and projects from understanding the operational problem through development, testing, rollout, and ongoing support. Design and build full-stack features, connecting frontend interfaces to backend services and data stores, with a clear understanding of how requests, authentication, and data move through the system.

description:
About the Team
DoorDash Labs is an independent team within DoorDash. We explore robotics and automation to transform last-mile logistics in the long term. If you have a passion for applying robotics solutions in a service used by millions of people, then we want to talk to you!
About the Role
As the Technician Lead, you will bridge the gap between high-level engineering goals and day-to-day shop floor execution. This is a "Player-Coach" role: you will spend 90-95% of your day as a hands-on contributor, executing high-level diagnostics and repairs alongside the team. You are responsible for ensuring the shift meets its daily output goals and uptime key results. While your primary focus is technical execution, you serve as the first point of escalation for the team and help ensure every technician is working efficiently and safely. You report to the Operations Manager, Service Operations, in our DoorDash Labs organization. This is an on-site role with expectations of 100% in-office in Mesa, AZ.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Lead the team to hit fleet uptime and repair goals while personally executing the most complex robotic diagnostics
Perform advanced repairs, including component-level troubleshooting and fixes on intricate electrical systems, control units, and associated hardware, with minimal supervision
Act as the process owner for the service center, creating and refining workflows that improve repair accuracy and shop efficiency
Provide a high level of dependability and accuracy in all technical documentation and shift handovers, setting the "Gold Standard" for the technician team

title: Senior Manufacturing Engineer (Remote)
description:
About MISUMI Americas
MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. By integrating a vast catalog of components with a world-class digital manufacturing platform, MISUMI Americas empowers engineers and procurement teams to accelerate innovation across the entire product lifecycle. With operations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, the company serves as a vital partner for the most innovative companies in the Americas.
The Senior Manufacturing Engineer role is a senior-level, hands-on manufacturing engineering position responsible for defining how custom parts are built and priced—reviewing manufacturability, generating competitive quotes, and providing design feedback that brings products to market faster. The role serves as a technical authority who helps raise the bar for costing and DFM (Design for Manufacturability) quality across regions.
MISUMI Americas serves three sets of customers—builders who order parts through us, manufacturing partners who make and assemble those parts, and our world-class sales professionals who rely on fast, accurate quoting and DFM support to win and serve accounts. This role sits at the interface of all three. As a senior member of the team, this person also coaches and mentors other engineers and partners closely with the Global Capability Center (GCC) Costing and DFM team, with room to grow their scope and influence over time.
Manufacturing Engineering & Quoting
● Release package review — Analyze models, drawings, parts lists, and other data to determine scope of work, manufacturing feasibility, requirements, and minimum lead time.
● Quoting — Combine engineering analysis with platform recommendations to generate quotes for builders or collaborate with external suppliers to determine the parameters needed to quote.
● Cost calculator generation — Use fabrication expertise and an understanding of process cost drivers to build cost calculators that bring quoting in-house for new service offerings.
● DFx feedback — Provide design-for-manufacturability and design-for-assembly feedback to builders, recommending changes that improve manufacturability, reduce part cost, or ease assembly.
● Automation feedback — Feed insights back to the quoting software team to improve the accuracy of automated quoting across manufacturing services.
● Drawing generation — Produce high-quality 2D drawings per ANSI/ASME Y14.5 standards.
Mentorship & Cross-Functional Collaboration
● Coaching & mentorship — Coach and mentor engineers on the US and GCC Costing and DFM teams, sharing fabrication and costing expertise to help them grow.
● Best practices & peer review — Help establish and document costing and DFM best practices, review work, and provide feedback that improves technical accuracy and consistency across regions.
● Cross-functional leadership — Lead through influence across engineering, sourcing, sales, quality, and software, aligning stakeholders on costing and DFM decisions without relying on direct authority.
● Dotted-line coordination — Guide and coordinate the technical work of engineers who do not report to this role (including GCC and cross-regional partners) and keep shared initiatives on track.
All employees are expected to maintain and contribute to the QMS.
● 4-year Mechanical Engineering degree or equivalent technical training.
● 5–10 years of relevant experience in manufacturing engineering, costing/DFM, or related custom mechanical hardware work.
● Hands-on experience across multiple custom mechanical manufacturing processes (sheet metal, urethane casting, injection molding, etc.); CNC machining and 3D printing experience is a must.
● Strong understanding of GD&T and conventional (coordinate) tolerancing, and deep knowledge of the manufacturability and limitations of common metals and plastics.
● Experience mentoring or coaching other engineers and acting as a technical resource; collaborating with offshore/GCC teams is a plus.
● Proven ability to lead through influence and coordinate cross-functional or dotted-line teams without direct reporting authority.
● Thrives with a high degree of autonomy—owns their workload end to end, exercises sound technical judgment independently, and drives decisions to closure in a remote environment with minimal oversight.
● Excellent written and verbal communication in English; comfortable working across multicultural, cross-functional teams.
● Meticulous and detail-oriented, with a documentation mindset. Experience with APQP/PPAP, IQ/OQ/PQ, EV/DV/PV, or NPI processes and/or PMP certification is a plus.
● Experience in AS9100, ISO 13485, or other highly regulated industries is highly recommended.
This position will work primarily remotely, computer-based work involving prolonged periods at a workstation reviewing CAD models and 2D drawings. Occasional visits to manufacturing partner facilities may involve a shop-floor environment (noise, moving equipment) and the ability to move about the facility. description:

We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.
The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.
Protecting Flexport's global operations and assets, enabling secure trade worldwide.
The opportunity:
Join Flexport's dynamic Compliance Program as the Senior Manager, Supply Chain Protection & Loss Intelligence. This critical role serves as the single point of accountability for both supply chain protection and loss prevention across Flexport's entire footprint — offices, fulfillment centers, and partner sites worldwide. The Manager will be responsible for protecting Flexport employees, visitors, assets, and facilities through the design and execution of security programs, while simultaneously driving a proactive loss prevention strategy across the Omni fulfillment network.
Day-to-day, this means managing a team of 50+ contracted security officers across multiple locations, overseeing electronic security infrastructure (CCTV, access control), conducting investigations, and managing the security ticketing system. Strategically, it means building the analytical foundation to identify loss trends and security gaps before they become incidents, authoring the policies and SOPs that standardize how Flexport protects its people and assets globally, and ensuring every new facility launches with security infrastructure and protocols in place from day one.
You will partner closely with operations, facilities, and leadership to design, implement, and scale security programs for existing and future locations, ensuring our people, assets, and reputation are safeguarded as Flexport rapidly expands into new markets. This is a unique opportunity to build a unified security strategy, moving beyond reactive incident management to a data-driven, proactive approach.

Develop and maintain security and loss prevention metrics, KPIs, and dashboards to measure program effectiveness across all facilities and regions
Analyze incident data to identify trends, loss patterns, root causes, and emerging risks — translating findings into actionable recommendations for leadership
Build reporting frameworks that support data-driven resource allocation, vendor performance evaluation, and security investment decisions
Provide regular analytical reports to senior management on security posture, loss prevention outcomes, and program ROI
Author, maintain, and enforce global security and loss prevention policies, ensuring consistency across all Flexport locations and compliance with local regulatory requirements in each jurisdiction
Develop and implement SOPs for key security scenarios (Active Shooter, Emergency Response, High Value Cage procedures, Product Disposal, etc.)
Create site-level security plans for new and existing facilities, tailored to local risk profiles and operational requirements
Design and deliver training programs across physical security and loss prevention topics (emergency response, office security, travel security, incident reporting, etc.)
Develop audit frameworks and LP checklists for site leads to execute on a recurring basis
Manage physical security programs across all Flexport facilities globally (offices, warehouses, and partner sites), including new locations as Flexport and the Omni fulfillment network expand into new markets
Lead security planning and infrastructure stand-up for new facilities and market entries, including site assessments, vendor selection, and system deployment
Administer and maintain electronic security systems, including CCTV surveillance and access control platforms, and evaluate new technology deployments
Serve as the crisis management coordinator, providing real-time threat assessments and coordinating emergency response across regions
Coordinate with HSE, HR, Legal, and Compliance on cross-functional security and safety matters
Drive loss prevention strategy and investigations for the Omni fulfillment network, including cargo theft, employee theft, unauthorized sellers, workplace violence, and empty package findings
Manage the security and loss prevention ticketing syste, including triaging, updating, and resolving tickets with accurate documentation
Identify root causes of supply chain losses and develop recommendations to reduce future risk
Review, collect, and preserve CCTV evidence to support investigations and legal proceedings
Manage third-party guard services across all locations, including oversight of 50+ security officers, performance tracking, and operational discipline
Manage relationships with security integrators and onboard new vendors as required for geographic expansion
Oversee vendor contracts, MSAs, and NDAs for all security-related service providers
Conduct regular business reviews with key vendors and evaluate service delivery against contractual obligations
You should have:
8+ years of progressive experience in a rike that combined physical security or loss prevention responsibilities with data analytics, policy development, or program design. Traditional security experience alone is not sufficient — this role requires a candidate who has built metrics programs, authored policies, or used data to drive security strategy.
Demonstrated ability to manage security operations across multiple locations and geographies, including hands-on experience with electronic security systems (CCTV, access control platforms).
Demonstrated experience building and analyzing security and loss prevention metrics, with comfort working in data platforms and translating incident data into actionable insights and executive-level reporting
Proven ability to author global policies, SOPs, security plans, and program documentation from scratch.
Experience managing third-party guard services and security vendor contracts, as well as conducting complex investigations (theft, workplace violence, supply chain security).
Excellent communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively with cross-functional teams including HR, Legal, Operations, and Compliance
An analytical mindset with attention to detail and the ability to identify root causes and solve problems

The opportunity to build and scale global security and loss prevention programs from the ground up in a rapidly expanding, tech-forward logistics company.
Direct impact on protecting Flexport's people, assets, and reputation across a vast international footprint.
A collaborative and innovative environment where your data-driven insights will directly inform strategic decisions.
