title: Head of Marketing - Bolingbrook, IL
description:

Formic is on a mission to reshape American manufacturing by making automation accessible to every factory. As labor constraints rise, costs increase, and global competition intensifies, automation is no longer optional for manufacturers that want to stay competitive.
We deliver automation through a Robotics-as-a-Service model that combines industrial robotics, proprietary software, and full-service support into a single, integrated solution. By removing the traditional barriers of cost, complexity, and risk, we enable manufacturers to deploy automation quickly and realize measurable gains in throughput, safety, and operational efficiency without large upfront capital investment.
Backed by leading investors including Lux Capital, Initialized Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and Mitsubishi HC Capital North America, Formic is scaling rapidly and building the foundation for a new era of high-performance, Made in America production.
About the team:
Formic's Marketing Team is the growth engine behind our commercial expansion. We move fast, experiment boldly, and build systems that scale. We work in close lockstep with Sales, RevOps, and Leadership to generate pipeline, sharpen our message, and get in front of the right manufacturers at the right time. This team is small, high-impact, and driven - and we're looking for someone who can match that energy.
About this role:
As our Head of Marketing, you will build, optimize, and lead a scalable engine for creating demand and qualified pipeline. You will own how Formic shows up in the market, how we identify and reach the manufacturers we can help, and how we turn that engagement into high quality opportunities for Sales.
This is a broad, hands-on role spanning Marketing, lead generation, Sales Development, and GTM Engineering and managing a team to deliver across those areas. You'll bring those capabilities together around a common goal: creating qualified pipeline and quantifying through data and insights what's driving it. As Formic grows, you'll help determine how the team and these capabilities evolve.
We're looking for someone who combines creativity with operating rigor. You'll set strategy, but you'll stay close enough to the work to understand what's actually happening. You'll establish clear priorities, ownership, and metrics, and make decisions based on results. When something works, you'll scale it. When it doesn't, you'll change it or stop doing it.
You'll also build and develop the team around you. That means setting clear expectations, delegating real ownership, coaching people to get better, and holding the team accountable for results. We want a leader who welcomes challenge, seeks out evidence that their assumptions may be wrong, and changes course when the data or the team tells them something different.
This is a builder role. One day you might be sharpening Formic's positioning; the next, reviewing pipeline performance with Sales, coaching an SDR, digging into why a campaign isn't converting, or working with a GTM Engineer to test a completely different way of reaching manufacturers. You should be equally comfortable asking "What should we try?" and "Did it work?"
We're not looking for someone to bring us a standard B2B marketing playbook or generate activity for activity's sake. We want someone who creates focus from ambiguity, turns experiments into learning, turns learning into repeatable systems, and can clearly connect the work of their organization to business results.
You will own the engine that feeds our sales and deployments.
In this role you will:
Own Brand & Marketing
Own Formic's marketing strategy and how we show up in the market.
Develop and continually sharpen our positioning, messaging, and story.
Translate Formic's technology, business model, and customer value proposition into messaging that resonates with manufacturers and their economic buyers.
Own content, creative, video, website, customer stories, events, campaigns, thought leadership, PR, product marketing, and other channels that build awareness and demand.
Develop differentiated messaging across industries, use cases, personas, and stages of the buying journey.
Turn customer outcomes, deployments, product capabilities, and what we're learning in the field into compelling content.
Build Formic's brand within manufacturing while ensuring our marketing investments support clear commercial objectives.
Own Demand & Pipeline Generation
Own the creation of qualified pipeline across Marketing, lead generation, SDR/outbound, ABM, events, paid, organic, partnerships, and emerging channels.
Establish clear pipeline goals and build repeatable systems to identify, engage, and qualify manufacturers that fit Formic's ideal customer profile, optimizing channel mix, conversion, and resources.
Lead and develop our Sales Development function, including targeting, prospecting strategy, messaging, sequencing, coaching, productivity, and performance.
Establish clear funnel definitions, ownership, lead routing, and follow-up processes to ensure every source of inbound and outbound interest is captured, acted upon, and effectively handed off to Sales.
Partner closely with Sales and RevOps on territory priorities, pipeline needs, lead quality, conversion, and feedback from the market.
Measure pipeline contribution, progression, conversion, and cost by source and channel, connecting marketing investments to closed-won revenue and informing where to invest, optimize, or stop.
Build Our GTM Innovation Capability
Lead our GTM Engineering capability, using AI, automation, data, enrichment, personalization, and emerging technologies to improve how we identify, reach, engage, and qualify potential customers.
Own the effectiveness and evolution of our marketing technology ecosystem, including CRM integrations, outbound platforms, lead routing, data quality, attribution, and reporting, in partnership with Sales and RevOps.
Build and optimize scalable systems for account identification, segmentation, prospecting, personalization, campaign execution, and lead management.
Evaluate existing tools and workflows, identifying opportunities to simplify, automate, integrate, consolidate, or eliminate work rather than defaulting to additional tools or headcount.
Drive disciplined experimentation across channels, technologies, data sources, and approaches, establishing clear hypotheses, measurable outcomes, and decisions about what to scale, change, or stop.
Ensure our GTM infrastructure is reliable, documented, and maintainable, with clear ownership, appropriate data governance, and minimal dependency on any single person or external partner.
Own the Funnel and the Numbers
Establish clear visibility into the entire funnel, from target account through qualified opportunity, pipeline progression, and revenue.
Define and own a focused set of metrics that measure pipeline creation, conversion, velocity, cost, channel effectiveness, and commercial impact.
Partner with Sales and RevOps to ensure reliable data, consistent reporting, and a shared understanding of performance.
Establish a disciplined operating cadence that translates performance insights into decisions about strategy, priorities, budget, and resources, holding the organization accountable for outcomes rather than activity.
Create Focus and Accountability
Translate broad company objectives into clear priorities, ownership, expectations, and measurable outcomes that connect the team's work to business goals.
Make disciplined decisions about priorities and resources, challenging assumptions, stopping initiatives that aren't delivering results, and adapting as we learn.
Stay close enough to the work to identify problems early, remove obstacles, and hold people accountable without becoming a bottleneck to execution.
Foster a culture of transparency, constructive challenge, and open communication about performance, priorities, tradeoffs, and lessons learned.
Establish accountability for external agencies, contractors, and technology partners, including deliverables, performance, costs, documentation, and continuity, while building sustainable processes that preserve institutional knowledge and support organizational change.
Build and Lead the Team
Lead and align a multidisciplinary organization spanning Marketing, content and creative, lead generation, Sales Development, and GTM Engineering around shared commercial goals.
Build a high-performing team by establishing clear expectations, delegating meaningful ownership, coaching and developing talent, and addressing performance gaps directly.
Assess existing capabilities, recognize and develop the strengths of the people already here, and determine what additional skills and resources we'll need as we grow.
Hire thoughtfully and build organizational capabilities that create leverage, rather than adding unnecessary layers or headcount.
Foster a culture of creativity, curiosity, accountability, experimentation, and continuous improvement, where people feel empowered to challenge assumptions and solve problems.
What Makes You a Great Fit:
Experience building and leading Marketing, Growth, Demand Generation, or similarly broad functions in high-growth B2B companies, with measurable commercial results.
A track record of building, improving, and scaling marketing and pipeline-generation systems, not simply inheriting and managing established operations.
Deep understanding of B2B demand generation, funnel economics, segmentation, conversion, attribution, and how Marketing, SDR, and Sales work together to create and convert pipeline.
Experience developing differentiated positioning and messaging for complex products, markets, and buying decisions.
Strong technical fluency and demonstrated experience evaluating, integrating, and optimizing marketing technology, data, automation, and AI-enabled GTM systems, with the ability to diagnose problems and make informed architectural decisions.
An AI-native mindset, with demonstrated ability to apply emerging technologies, experiment rigorously, evaluate results, and turn successful approaches into scalable capabilities.
Strong people leadership, including building and developing teams, delegating meaningful ownership, addressing performance gaps, and leading effectively through growth and organizational change.
An operating style that combines creativity, analytical rigor, intellectual flexibility, and accountability, with the judgment to challenge assumptions, make difficult tradeoffs, and change course when evidence warrants it.
The ability to operate strategically and tactically, creating clarity from ambiguity, communicating effectively across functions, and staying close enough to execution to understand and solve problems.
Bonus points if you have:
Experience in manufacturing, industrial automation, robotics, industrial technology, or similarly complex B2B markets with long sales cycles and multiple decision-makers.
Experience directly building or leading SDR organizations, including account-based and territory-based outbound strategies.
Experience building or leading GTM Engineering, Growth Engineering, or similar technical growth capabilities.
What Success Looks Like
Within your first year, Formic has a marketing and pipeline-generation engine that we understand, measure, and know how to scale.
We know who we should target, how to reach them, which messages resonate, which channels create qualified opportunities, what those opportunities cost, and where we should invest next.
There is clear ownership across the funnel. Marketing, lead generation, Sales Development, and GTM Engineering operate as one connected organization, with a tight feedback loop into Sales. The team knows what matters and what it's accountable for.
Experiments have hypotheses and measurable outcomes. Successful ideas become repeatable systems. Unsuccessful ones produce learning and stop consuming resources. Decisions about priorities, budget, and headcount are grounded in results.
Our marketing and GTM infrastructure is reliable, integrated, and well understood. We have confidence in our data, clear accountability for lead management, and systems that the team can operate and improve independently. Technology and vendor decisions are deliberate, economically justified, and aligned with our commercial priorities.
Most importantly, Sales has a consistent and growing flow of qualified opportunities, and we can explain what is creating them.
That's the engine you'll own.
Our Total Rewards:
At Formic, we believe people do their best work when they feel supported both professionally and personally. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits and perks package for full-time, U.S.-based team members, including:
Equity in Formic: Participate in our stock option program and share in the success of a fast-growing start-up backed by leading global investors
Competitive & Uncapped Commission Structure: Designed to reward performance and impact in commission-eligible roles
Comprehensive Healthcare Coverage: Medical, dental, and vision insurance through Blue Cross Blue Shield and Unum, with 99% of employee premiums covered and 75% coverage for dependents, with optional buy-up plans available
Additional Insurance Benefits: FSA and DCFSA, life insurance, short-term disability, and long-term disability through Unum, all 100% employer-paid
Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Fully funded by Formic, offering support when you need it most
Paid Parental Leave Program: Up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave
Company-sponsored 401(k): Invest in your future with our company-facilitated retirement savings plan
Home Office Stipend: A one-time allowance for fully remote and hybrid employees to support an at-home or on-the-road work setup
Monthly Cell Phone Reimbursement: Monthly stipend toward personal phone and internet expenses
Flexible Time Off: Take the time you need, when you need it, supported by our flexible PTO policy
Compensation Philosophy
Formic’s pay and equity packages are thoughtfully benchmarked against peer companies at a similar growth stage. Equity represents a meaningful part of our mutual investment: when Formic succeeds, so do you.
Final offers are customized based on experience, geographic location, market considerations, and a candidate’s preferred balance of cash and equity. Our goal is to attract and reward top talent who will have significant impact, and we are open to thoughtful discussions to align on the right structure.
Compensation Range: $145,000 — $220,000 USD What we look for:
We’re building this company from the ground up, and every person we hire has an outsized impact on our culture, performance, and trajectory. While each team member brings unique strengths and perspectives, we look for people who align with our Operating Principles and embody them in action. If this sounds like you, Formic may be the right place for you!
Fearless Optimism: You make bold bets and default optimistic. You believe in the mission, aren’t paralyzed by risk, and fear inaction more than failure. You see ambiguity as opportunity and bring energy to building what doesn’t yet exist.
Create the Magic: You absorb complexity so customers don’t have to. Whether your customer is external or internal, you focus on delivering experiences that are clear, fast, value-added, and outcome-driven. You don’t say “not my job.” You make things work.
Today, Not Tomorrow: You have a bias to action. You close the loop. You take extreme ownership. You understand that speed compounds, and you don’t confuse activity with results.
Seek Truth: You think from first principles. You value data over ego and strong opinions loosely held. You’re willing to challenge assumptions, including your own, in pursuit of the best answer.
Made of Rubber: You are resolute and adaptable. When things break or priorities shift, you rebound stronger. You treat setbacks as learning moments and move forward with grit.
One Formic: You operate without silos. You practice radical helpfulness, document clearly, and make clean handoffs. You assume positive intent and prioritize team success over individual credit.

Formic is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion or religious creed, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, marital status, family or parental status, disability, military or veteran status, or any other basis protected by law. All employment decisions are based on a person’s merit, business needs, and role requirements. If you require further accommodations or have questions regarding accessibility of our roles, please reach out to  careers@formic.co .
AI Use:
At Formic, fairness and transparency are at the heart of our hiring process. We use AI-powered tools in some interviews to help our teams evaluate candidate responses, but all final hiring decisions are made by humans. You can learn more about how AI is used in our recruitment process by reviewing our AI Hiring Disclosure linked  here .

As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
You will join Future Forward, Intuitive's advanced concepts group, and report to an engineering lead on the team building AI for the next generation of robotic-assisted surgery. You will own an open-ended research and prototyping project in areas such as supervised autonomy and automation for robotic-assisted surgery, and AI that helps care teams deliver care more consistently and efficiently. The work draws on computer vision, generative AI, robotics, and agentic AI, and we will shape the exact project with you based on your background and the team's priorities. Own an open-ended research and prototyping project, scoped with your mentor.
Explore how computer vision, generative AI, and agentic AI can be applied to new problems in surgery and the operating room.
Build working prototypes and evaluate them against clear baselines.
Work closely with researchers, engineers, and clinical experts.
Share your results through documentation and a final presentation and contribute to publications or patent filings where results warrant it.

Research or applied experience in at least one of computer vision, generative AI, robotics or autonomy, or agentic AI (LLM agents and tool use).
Strong Python skills and hands-on experience with a deep learning framework such as PyTorch.
A track record of taking a loosely defined problem to a result, shown through publications, open-source work, or projects others have used.

Clear written and verbal communication with both technical and non-technical audiences.

Publications at leading venues such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CoRL, RSS, ICRA, or IROS.

Primary Function of Position
The HEOR Intern will join Intuitive’s Future Forward Medical Affairs team for a 10–12 week summer internship, reporting to the Staff Epidemiologist, Future Forward Medical Affairs. The intern will own a defined, scoped real-world evidence project, using administrative claims data and reimbursement coding (CPT/HCPCS, ICD-10-CM/PCS, MS-DRG) to characterize patient populations, procedure volumes, healthcare resource utilization, and costs for a technology in development. Real-World Data Analysis: With guidance from senior team members, conduct a retrospective claims-based analysis to characterize patient populations, estimate procedure volumes, and describe utilization, outcomes, and costs relevant to a Future Forward pipeline technology.

Study Planning & Programming: Contribute to a brief study protocol and statistical analysis plan; write, document, and quality-check analytic code, partnering with the team’s data scientist on shared data pipelines.
Evidence Review: Conduct a targeted literature review to inform study design, benchmark findings against published evidence, and surface evidence gaps for the technology under study.
Economic Modeling Support: Where relevant, translate claims-based estimates (e.g., procedure volumes, event rates, costs) into inputs for budget impact or other economic models, and support model development or validation.
Communication: Summarize findings in clear visualizations and slides; deliver a final presentation to Future Forward leadership; contribute to a draft abstract where findings warrant.
Required Skills and Experience
Hands-on experience with reimbursement coding systems (CPT/HCPCS, ICD-10-CM/PCS, and MS-DRG), gained through dissertation research, research-assistant work, or prior employment, including using codes to define cohorts, procedures, and outcomes.
Demonstrated experience analyzing at least one large administrative claims or hospital database (e.g., Medicare MedPAR/SAF, MarketScan, Optum Clinformatics, Premier, PearlDiver, Komodo Health, or similar), from data extraction and cleaning through analysis.

Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to translate technical analysis for non-specialist audiences.
Comfortable working on a defined deliverable under the guidance of senior team members, with the independence to drive it to completion within the internship period.
Intellectual curiosity and comfort with ambiguity; this team works on problems that are not yet fully defined.

Current enrollment in a Health Economics, Health Outcomes/Services Research, Health Policy, Pharmaceutical Outcomes Research, Epidemiology, Biostatistics, or related degree-seeking program at the Doctorate (PhD) level.

None

Experience developing or adapting budget impact models or other health economic models (e.g., cost-effectiveness, cost-consequence) in Excel, consistent with ISPOR good-practice guidelines.

Recommend a suggested algorithm / experimental setup moving forward (beyond the internship) based on experimental results, and present findings to the broader team.

The Reimbursement Operations & Field Market Access lead is the execution engine of the U.S. HEMA organization. This role is the closest link to the sales and marketing organization and serves as the primary tactical interface with providers, payers, and field teams.
This is both a payer-facing and provider-facing role. On the payer side, this person develops value dossiers, manages payer advisory boards, and supports key account engagement. On the provider side, this person generates billing guides, fields customer reimbursement questions, develops provider education materials, and supports all field logistics related to coding implementation.
In Phase 1, this role carries both midstream and downstream responsibilities—from code acquisition and payment policy implementation through to field collateral generation and customer support. Code Implementation Logistics: Manage all field logistics associated with the implementation of new or existing CPT, HCPCS, and ICD-10 codes. Coordinate with provider sites to ensure smooth adoption of coding changes and cost capture.
Sales & Marketing Support: Generate evidence-driven, compliant field collateral in direct support of the sales and marketing organization.

As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
The Senior Project Manager, Multiport leads and organizes a diverse set of activities of the Program Management Office (PMO) group within the New Product Development organization. The PMO group is responsible for leading cross functional teams in new product development and continuation engineering initiatives, and consists of project managers, program managers and project coordinators.
The Senior Project Manager, Multiport orchestrates the activities of their project teams to deliver compelling final product designs within demanding product release schedules. This role will have a focus on complex surgical robotic instrumentation (e.g. stapling, vessel sealing devices), including bringing new innovative technology and design improvements to global markets. The Senior Project Manager, Multiport must be highly organized and detail-oriented, and interact fluidly and effectively with numerous individuals and departments. The Senior Project Manager, PMO will have a close working relationship with the Design Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Quality, Regulatory, Clinical, Human Factors, Technical Publications, Training, Service, Finance, and Marketing departments, as well as other program and project managers.
Essential Job Duties
Project Leadership & Execution
Lead and drive a portfolio of complex, cross-functional product development projects from conception to manufacturing stability, with an initial focus on disposable surgical robotic instrumentation
Ensure Design Control processes are followed per relevant procedures
Ensure that complex, high-value Business Unit projects are properly scoped, resourced, and communicated to minimize risk, deliver on-time and on-budget Function as the primary point-of-contact for key leaders and stakeholders across the organization
Organize and manage team meetings, design review meetings, and phase gate review meetings
Create and maintain project schedules
Develop and monitor project budgets
Support resource demand planning for project teams, including estimating project work efforts, needs, roles, and responsibilities
Lead large, distributed cross-functional teams to execute effectively
Plan and track the creation of design history documents for projects by the project teams
Facilitate best practices sharing and feedback to the PMO organization and seek areas of process improvements
Strategy & Prioritization
Support in defining and aligning project goals with business unit and corporate objectives; organize and prioritize the work of teams to accomplish those objectives
Work closely with Product Development Franchise leaders to develop plans to meet strategic objectives
Contribute to product prioritization decisions by providing data and analysis from current and past projects
Cross-Functional Collaboration
Support team members including functional managers across the business to plan and execute the activities required to achieve project goals
Work closely with Design, Manufacturing, Marketing, Regulatory, and Quality organizations to ensure input and representation in the development process
Work with Operations and Manufacturing management to determine strategies for product cut-ins and roll-ins
Coordinate effectively with other project managers who are driving overall product development programs to understand project goals, scope, timelines, and help functional managers negotiate resources and schedules
Communication & Stakeholder Management
Communicate project priorities, key project deliverables, milestones and project risk broadly and effectively— including within the PMO team, to all cross-functional team members, to business unit management, and to shared services management
Build strong formal and informal communication channels to keep all stakeholders informed of accurate and timely information
Provide feedback to team members regarding performance and requirements
Required Skills and Experience
Highly passionate about delivering improved surgical solutions to patients, with a proven ability to coordinate and drive cross-functional teams
Strong project/program management, planning, decision making, negotiating, communication, and change management skills
Experience and skills developing medical device products through Design Controls with a high level of complexity, including consumables with demonstrated success at product launches as a result of completing product development cycles
Proven ability to lead, influence and work well at all levels of an organization and in a cross functional team environment
Experience with leading people within a project team that includes many engineering disciplines, including clinical, mechanical, electrical, and software
Exceptional aptitude for cultivating collaboration across department boundaries and influence cross-functional teams without formal authority to ensure project success
Proven success recognizing critical issues with the ability to react quickly under pressure, and drive issues to closure by providing coordinated direction
High attention to detail and proven ability to manage multiple, competing priorities simultaneously; must work well under pressure, be flexible, and meet deadlines
Excellent communication (written, verbal), presentation and documentation skills and high emotional intelligence
Results-driven self-starter with high energy, initiative, accountability and a collaborative team-first attitude
Self-directed and resourceful with a strong work ethic; able to navigate conflict and drive issues to resolution
Comfortable with ambiguity; able to manage multiple projects simultaneously
Ability to lead a large number of people on a variety of programs
Committed to continuously improving product development and program management processes
Required Education and Training
BS degree (or equivalent experience) in a scientific / engineering field plus 8 years experience leading teams in the development and commercialization of medical device products. Or similarly, MS degree plus 6 years experience. Advanced degree is a plus.

Work with all phases of the product development lifecycle including idea generation, concept development and testing, design, implementation, validation, and transfer
Working knowledge of manufacturing, engineering, product strategy and business management
Experience in studying tradeoffs between product desirability, feasibility, and viability
Demonstrates ability to synthesize data, set actionable goals and drive metrics and execution

We are looking for a leader who knows what great looks like to head Global Enterprise (Indirect) Procurement at Intuitive. This is a fantastic opportunity to join a leader in robotic-assisted surgery with a mission to improve outcomes for patients. Procurement plays a critical role in that mission by ensuring the people, services, technology and facilities behind our work are sourced with excellence, integrity and care.
It is also an opportunity to join a fantastic team with a great culture that focuses on the how as much as on the what. We want a leader who can build a compelling vision for the function, leads with integrity and humility, and is passionate about developing and caring for the team.
The Sr. Director is accountable for the global indirect spend portfolio and for building a best-in-class procurement function. The role drives measurable value through strategic sourcing, category management and supplier partnerships, makes buying simple for stakeholders, strengthens compliance and risk management, and uses data and AI to raise the function's impact.
Essential Job Duties
The Sr. Director, Head of Global Enterprise Procurement leads the global indirect procurement function, partners closely with Finance, Legal, IT, Operations and Commercial leaders, and is a trusted advisor to the executive team on spend, suppliers and third-party risk. The Sr. Director will:
Vision, Strategy and Leadership
Develop and communicate a clear multi-year vision and roadmap for a best-in-class function, including operating model, capabilities, technology and talent.
Lead, mentor and develop the team across procurement operations, sourcing, contracts, and travel and events, with clear performance measurement, career paths and succession plans.
Build an engaged, accountable team that acts with the highest integrity and cares about the how as much as the what.
Category Management and Strategic Sourcing
Own multi-year category strategies for all indirect spend, such as software and technology, professional services, contingent labor, facilities and MRO, marketing and logistics, built in partnership with business stakeholders.
Use in-depth spend analysis and company-wide purchasing volume to lead sourcing initiatives, negotiations and supply agreements that maximize cost, service, quality and supplier capability.
Shape demand upstream through standardization, policy and user education, and track value beyond savings, including stakeholder satisfaction, innovation and risk resilience.
Supplier Relationship and Risk Management
Rationalize the supplier base and build long-term partnerships with strategic suppliers, supported by a supplier performance and business review program.
Partner with Legal, Information Security, Quality and Compliance to manage supplier risk (financial, cyber, concentration, geopolitical and disruption) and to ensure contracts address regulatory and legal requirements.
Procurement Operations, Technology and Compliance
Continuously improve the source-to-pay lifecycle, including intake, sourcing, contracting, purchasing and payables, to reduce cost to serve, ease the stakeholder experience, and increase spend under management.
Champion data-driven decisions with dashboards and metrics for savings, compliance and customer satisfaction, and apply automation and AI where they add value.
Work with Accounting, Accounts Payable and FP&A for seamless procure-to-pay, and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, SOPs, DOPs and SOX.
Travel and Events
Manage global travel and event services, working with Sales, Marketing, Finance and other stakeholders to provide exceptional service, minimize cost, and maximize user efficiency while providing an experience that reflects the company's culture.
Required Skills and Experience
15+ years of progressive procurement experience, including 10+ years in indirect procurement with global responsibility and 5+ years leading teams in a large, publicly traded or comparable environment.
Proven track record of delivering measurable value through category management and strategic sourcing, and of building or elevating a procurement organization with a clear vision and strong talent.
Demonstrated ability to develop high-performing teams, with a passion for developing and caring for people and a leadership style grounded in integrity and humility.
High commercial and financial acumen, with the gravitas to influence at the executive level and partner with Finance, Legal, IT and business leaders.
Seasoned negotiator with experience in complex, multi-million-dollar, multi-year agreements across diverse categories.
Strong data analytics skills, with a point of view on how AI and automation can transform procurement.
Expertise in source-to-pay systems and orchestration tools (Coupa preferred) and knowledge of procurement compliance, including SOX.
Excellent communication skills, able to translate complex sourcing issues into clear terms for suppliers, peers and senior leaders.
Medical device, life sciences or other regulated industry experience is helpful.
Willingness to travel 15-20%, including to Atlanta, Mexico, Europe and Asia Pacific.
Required Education and Training
Bachelor's degree in supply chain, business, finance, engineering or equivalent.
MBA or professional procurement certification (for example CPSM or CIPS) preferred.

title: Staff Mechanical Design Engineer
description:

As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
At Intuitive, we believe that minimally invasive care is life-enhancing care. By combining ingenuity and intelligent technology, we expand the potential of physicians to heal without constraints. We are looking for team members with exceptional character who have the capacity to simplify complex problems and the energy to deliver solutions urgently to our patients. Intuitive Accessories are the interface between all aspects of the da Vinci system and enable safe and effective robot-assisted surgery. Our customers interact directly with Accessories in every surgical procedure, and they serve a critical role in customer satisfaction and patient outcomes. The Staff Mechanical Design Engineer for Single-Port (SP) Accessories will support development
and production of existing and new products. This position requires a hands-on, technically strong engineer to dive deep into solving engineering challenges, and to provide high-level assessment of risks and opportunities. Projects will include a mix of sustaining existing products and new product development, including improvements for cost savings and manufacturability to enable significant volume growth, enhancements to increase customer satisfaction, and improving reliability.
Essential Job Duties
• Drive Design efforts to optimize performance, manufacturability and reliability of existing and future Da Vinci SP Accessories.
• Develop components and product mechanical drawings in a regulated environment for high volume manufacturing processes, including plastic injection molding, thermoset compression molding, extrusion, and machining.
• Design for manufacturing and automation, sterilization processes, and biocompatibility.
• Work cross-functionally with Manufacturing Engineers, Systems Analysts, Clinical Development Engineers, Human Factors Engineers, and Supplier Engineers.
• Review and understand product functional requirements and design specifications.
• Provide mechanical engineering sustaining support for resolution of manufacturing and field issues.
• Investigate and determine root cause of design, manufacturing, or material issues.
• Research, understand, and design to relevant product-specific international standards.
• Develop, implement, test, and document solutions that meet clinical, functional, and product requirements.
• Perform and document risk analyses (FMEA) and implement effective mitigations, following design control processes.
• Help identify and develop vendors to manufacture components.
• Develop initial fixtures and processes to assemble components.
• Develop product and component verification testing and product validation testing
• Support production of final product by troubleshooting process and component problems
• Provide engineering support to Manufacturing, Materials, Test Engineering, and Service to facilitate transfer of
designs.
• Develop, implement, test and document solutions for these opportunities according to corporate standard and departmental operating procedures
• Mentor other engineers and champion best practices for mechanical design
Required Skills and Experience
• Proficiency using CAD to design and document mechanisms; SolidWorks strongly preferred
• Good communication and documentation skills
• Experience in designing high volume consumable medical products
• Strong working knowledge of GD&T
• Experience with complex interface compatibility and tolerance analysis
• Demonstrated knowledge of high-volume component manufacturing processes (including injection molding, plastics films, extrusions, thermoforming, and plastic bonding methods)
• Demonstrated knowledge of materials (preferably plastics, silicones, polyurethanes, isoprenes) and material properties. Ability to apply knowledge of engineering materials and component selection criteria to product designs through strong concept development, design analysis, hands-on prototyping, and reliability testing skills.
• Demonstrated ability to think at a systems level, interface between multiple design groups, and negotiate conflicting requirements.
• Comfortable with all phases of the product development lifecycle including design, implementation, debug, verification, qualification, and transfer.
• A passion for solving tough technical problems - Strong mechanical intuition and persistence to drill down to pinpoint root cause of problems, solving problems using fundamental principles.
• Ability to communicate effectively (written, oral) across functions, including presenting to a technical audience
• Prior experience working in medical device or other regulated industry
Required Education and Training
• Minimum education: BS in Mechanical Engineering required, MSME preferred. Biomedical or other engineering discipline may be acceptable with appropriate mechanical experience.
• Minimum 12 years of hardware product design experience preferred with undergraduate degree; minimum 8 years with graduate degree
Working Conditions
• Ability to lift 30 lbs. without assistance.
Preferred Skills and Experience (As applicable - Specific skills, knowledge, and experience that
are not required to perform the job, but are desirable to have)
• Comfortable operating machine shop tools/equipment, Rapid prototype equipment (3-d printers, laser cutters etc.), measurement and test equipment
• Knowledge in additional manufacturing processes such as extrusion, blow molding, ultrasonic welding, RF welding, heat staking, and laser welding
• Comfortable with concepts of design input, design output, traceability, and risk analysis
• Ability to handle ambiguity effectively and oversee multiple projects at once
• Knowledge of ISO requirements and GMP guidelines. Experience with FDA regulations and medical device design control a strong plus
• Experience leading departmental or cross-functional projects/initiatives from concept through completion
• Knowledge of sterilization methods, biocompatibility, and packaging of medical devices

Off-Line testing
On-line testing

title: Receiving Operator - Days
description:
Job Description:
Job Title: Receiving Operator
Shift: 6am – 6:30pm (223 Rotation)
Location: Fremont, Nebraska, USA
Being a Mars Associate is all about opportunity.  The opportunity to do the kind of challenging, interesting work that shapes the world’s best-loved brands.  To work with real purpose, supported by talented, friendly people from all sorts of different backgrounds.  Access the tools, training and experience you need to have a positive impact on our business, on the planet, and most importantly on your own career.  Being a Mars associate is more than a job.  It’s the opportunity to start your tomorrow today.
Job Purpose/Overview:
This role is responsible for performing all reception and unloading operations for raw materials coming into the manufacturing facility. This position will also handle master sanitation activities for the area and perform required inventory tasks.
Key Responsibilities:
Perform receiving and unloading of all raw materials (bulks, liquids, super sacks, bags).
Operate forklifts and other equipment to offload and store materials.
Manage and sign delivery documentation, noting any quality or quantity discrepancies.
Collaborate with the supply coordinator on inbound receiving priorities.
Accurately maintain the Warehouse Management System (WMS) and report any stock discrepancies.
Perform cyclical and period-end inventory counts of raw ingredients.
Conduct equipment verifications, record keeping, and first-level maintenance.
Uphold food safety standards and adhere to site Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs).
Execute sanitation duties as required by the Master Sanitation Schedule, following lock-out/tag-out procedures.
Promote a positive and high-quality team environment.
Qualifications:
Must be 18 years of age or older.
High school diploma, GED, or equivalent.
Willing and able to work varying shifts, schedules, and overtime.
Ability to work with minimal supervision and as part of a team.
Strong communication skills in English.
Preferred: 1 year of work experience in manufacturing or a related technical discipline.
Preferred: Competency in computer software, including MS Office, email, and inventory (WMS) systems.
Preferred: Knowledge of inventory control principles and ability to operate a forklift or scissor lift.
Physical/Environmental Requirements:
Ability to stand on a concrete floor for extended periods.
Must wear proper personal protective equipment (PPE).
Capable of bending, stooping, twisting, turning, reaching, and climbing stairs.
Ability to lift up to 55 lbs.
Must be able to adapt to temperature and environmental extremes (hot, cold, dust, dirt, chemicals).
Military Crosswalk: Transferable Skills
This position aligns well with the skills and experience gained in numerous military occupational specialties. Veterans bring valuable expertise in logistics, inventory management, and operations.
Relevant Military Experience:
The skills required for the Receiving Operator role are commonly found in the following (but not limited to) military logistics and supply fields:
Army: Automated Logistical Specialist (92A)
Unit Supply Specialist (92Y)
Cargo Specialist (88H)
Petroleum Supply Specialist (92F)
Air Force: Logistics Plans (2G0X1)
Materiel Management (2S0X1)
Air Transportation (2T2X1)
Navy: Logistics Specialist (LS)
Culinary Specialist (Submarine, Supply) (CSS)
Marine Corps: Logistics/Embarkation Specialist (0431)
Warehouse Clerk (3051)
Packaging Specialist (3052)
Coast Guard: Storekeeper (SK)
Transferable Skills:
Inventory Management: Experience with tracking, counting, and managing stock levels is directly applicable to maintaining the WMS and performing inventory cycles.
Logistics & Supply Chain: Military personnel are experts in receiving, storing, and issuing materials, which is the core function of this role.
Heavy Equipment Operation: Many military roles involve operating forklifts and other material handling equipment.
Attention to Detail: The military instills a high degree of precision, crucial for verifying shipments and maintaining accurate records.
Safety Compliance: Adherence to strict safety protocols, such as handling hazardous materials or following operational procedures, is a fundamental military skill.
Teamwork and Discipline: Working effectively within a team to achieve a common goal is a hallmark of military service.
We encourage veterans and transitioning service members with experience in these or related fields to apply.
Education & Professional Qualifications
Be 18 years of age or older
Have a high school diploma, GED, or equivalent education
Must be willing and able to work and accept varying shifts and schedules
Ability to understand and effectively communicate in the English language
Knowledge / Experience
3+ years of manufacturing experience operating a variety of machines
2 years of work experience within manufacturing, or a technical and/or trade discipline
Demonstrated competency in computer and pc software including MS Office and email
Knowledge of inventory control principles
Ability to operate a forklift and scissor lift

title: Regional Distributor Manager, U.S.
description:
Job Description:
Champion Petfoods is expanding! We are excited to announce we are looking for a Regional Distributor Manager, U.S. to join our rapidly growing company.
Champion Petfoods is an award-winning pet food maker with a reputation of trust spanning 35+ years. Founded in a small town in Alberta, Canada, Champion – with its ORIJEN® and ACANA® brands – is a key player in the global premium pet food industry across three major geographic regions.
We would love to hear from you if you are passionate about personal and professional growth and see yourself as a key player contributing to our continued success as an award-winning company.
Here's the Scoop – Summary
The Regional Distributor Manager, U.S. is accountable for delivering sales growth, market share expansion, distribution gains, and execution excellence through Champion's distributor partners within an assigned region.
Reporting to the Director, U.S. Sales, Neighborhood Pet, this role serves as the primary business lead for distributor performance and development.
The Regional Distributor Manager translates national sales strategy into regional execution plans, ensuring distributors and their sales organizations are aligned to Champion's priorities and growth objectives.
This position drives business results through distributor leadership, joint business planning, retailer engagement, sales capability development, and disciplined performance management.
Success in this role is achieved by building strong distributor partnerships, improving execution at retail, developing distributor sales teams, and delivering profitable growth throughout the region.
This is a fully remote position, which will ideally sit near Boulder (CO), Dallas (TX), Phoenix (AZ) or Southern California (CA). Expect 40-50% of travel within assigned geography.
Responsibilities:
Distributor Performance Ownership
Own sales, distribution, and execution result across assigned distributor partners and territories.
Hold distributors accountable to annual sales targets, distribution objectives, promotional programs, and strategic growth priorities.
Monitor distributor performance through established KPIs and implement corrective action plans when required.
Regularly evaluate distributor effectiveness, market coverage, resource allocation, and return on investment.
Distributor Strategy & Business Planning
Develop and execute Joint Business Plans with distributor partners aligned to national sales objectives and growth strategies.
Identify opportunities to increase market penetration, distribution points, retailer productivity, and share growth.
Lead annual planning, forecasting, and business review processes with assigned distributors.
Align distributor investments and resources to maximize commercial performance and customer impact.
Driving Execution Through Distributor Sales Teams
Influence, coach, and develop Distributor Sales Representatives (DSRs) to improve execution and sales effectiveness.
Conduct regular market visits to evaluate retail execution, merchandising standards, assortment compliance, and promotional effectiveness.
Deliver sales training, product education, and business development support to distributor sales organizations.
Ensure execution excellence against merchandising, pricing, promotional, and distribution objectives.
Retail Customer Development
Partner with key regional and independent retail customers to support growth, distribution expansion, and customer satisfaction.
Conduct customer business reviews and identify opportunities to strengthen Champion's market position.
Support distributor teams in developing retailer-specific growth strategies and action plans.
Build trusted relationships that position Champion as a strategic partner.
Forecasting, Analytics & Financial Management
Maintain accurate regional forecasts and provide timely updates on risks and opportunities.
Manage trade investments and promotional spending to maximize ROI and profitability.
Analyze sales performance, market trends, customer results, and distributor productivity to identify opportunities for growth.
Provide regular business updates and recommendations to the Director, U.S. Sales.
Market Leadership
Represent Champion Petfoods at industry events, trade shows, distributor meetings, and customer engagements.
Deliver insights regarding competitive activity, consumer trends, market dynamics, and emerging opportunities.
Partner cross-functionally with Marketing, Finance, Supply Chain, and Customer Service to ensure successful execution of business initiatives.
Key Accountabilities
The Regional Distributor Manager will be measured on:
Regional sales and profitability growth
Distributor performance against annual operating plan
Distribution gains and market penetration
Retail execution and merchandising compliance
Forecast accuracy
Trade investment ROI
Distributor sales force capability development
Regional customer growth and retention
Achievement of strategic business plan objectives
What are we looking for?
Bachelor's degree in Business, Sales, Marketing, or a related field.
5+ years of progressive sales experience within the pet industry, consumer packaged goods, or a related distribution-driven environment.
Demonstrated success managing distributor relationships and driving growth through indirect sales channels.
Proven ability to develop and execute business plans that deliver revenue growth, distribution gains, and improved customer performance.
Strong financial and commercial acumen, including forecasting, budgeting, business analysis, and ROI management.
Experience influencing and developing sales teams without direct reporting authority.
Excellent relationship-building, negotiation, and communication skills.
Ability to analyze market data and translate insights into actionable growth strategies.
Highly collaborative, self-motivated leader who thrives in a fast-paced and entrepreneurial environment.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and sales reporting tools.
Ability to travel approximately 40-50% within assigned geography.
Why You'll Succeed
You take ownership of results and hold yourself and partners accountable.
You know how to win through distributors and indirect sales channels.
You build strong partnerships while maintaining high performance expectations.

Responsibilities
Critical Environment Culture
May travel up to 25%, typically domestically for training and/or supporting another site. May work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.
Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting up to 25lbs / 11kg without assistance. Occasional lifting 25-50lbs / 11-22.5kg with lift assistance. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.
Understands, follows, and ensures safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures are met, to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance to applicable Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations, and Microsoft requirements. Recognizes safe versus unsafe working conditions and responds accordingly (e.g., stop/pause tasks, stand down vendors where necessary). Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed and promotes a safe working culture to empower less experienced team members. Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Proactively ensures safety and security requirements are followed and met for the work of themselves and others.
Equipment and Systems Maintenance
Provides and/or assigns team members to provide necessary escort to third-party contractors, sub-contractors, vendors, and service providers on site for all procedure levels of risk (LOR). May take part in getting third-party work underway (e.g., making sure systems are properly energized/deenergized), ensuring the work is started and completed in a safe manner in accordance with standard practices, procedures, and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations. Ensures work performed by suppliers/vendors is performed to scope, all documentation is performed correctly, and escalates as appropriate. Engages to address and resolve circumstances when supplier/vendor work has been stopped to address potential and/or identified concerns. Coordinates and/or assigns team members to coordinate across all LOR applicable to preventative and/or corrective maintenance. Identifies and recommends procedure corrections if/when errors are detected or when appropriate. Coordinates and schedules supplier/vendor on-site activities. Coordinates with vendor to schedule maintenance and determines availability of equipment/parts, as directed. Resolves or escalates observed vendor quality issues. Reviews and approves vendor supplier field service reports, invoices, and work orders.
Prepares and submits highly complex reports as assigned following preexisting scripts and templates, or using ad hoc methods required to support trending and analysis (e.g., Root Cause Analysis [RCA] reports) and may review prior reports delivered by less experienced team members. Develops methods of operating procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and/or digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for highly complex and/or interdependent equipment and disciplines to ensure safe and reliable execution. Reviews completed work using approved tools and procedural templates from less experienced technicians for accuracy and completeness. Provides assignment and completion oversight of team members for mandatory, technical, and procedural training material. Assigns and oversees procedure development and reporting to team members. Analyzes findings from reports and documents observations.
Guides, oversees, and performs various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs for multiple disciplines and multiple equipment types of increasing complexity with no supervision, while serving as a subject matter expert for one discipline - in consideration of Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Method Statement of Work (MSOW), or varying permit requirements. Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Provides consultation to colleagues on maintenance and repairs through deep understanding of equipment, systems and their interrelations. Follows recommended maintenance schedules. Oversees everyday, complex, large-scale tasks for a single discipline or equipment across disciplines. Ensures follow up action items are addressed in a timely manner. Masters the maintenance of all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner and understands levels of risk (LORs) associated with varying types of maintenance across all disciplines and supports team members with subject matter expertise. Plans, coordinates, and presents maintenance items for review and approval in their area of responsibility.
Processes method statement of work (MSOW) documents. Leads and provides guidance on coordinating activities and establishing associated schedules with contractors. Performs inspections of equipment in a facility. Participates in testing and commissioning activities. Advises engineer partners or project management colleagues on project scope process or execution methodology. Presents for review and approval MSOW in their area of responsibility.
Acts as a subject matter expert, performing troubleshooting independently for multiple equipment, systems, subsystems, and component types. Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Determines when troubleshooting efforts are deemed adequate and communicates or escalates to suppliers, engineers, or more experienced colleagues as needed. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment in all disciplines work and how to troubleshoot to subsystem level. Provides consultation to less experienced colleagues with troubleshooting systems and problems. Ensures troubleshooting completion paths are escalated appropriately and successfully by their team members. Oversees and advises their team members on troubleshooting systems and/or investigates root causes.
Equipment and Systems Operations
Takes part in, and oversees team in the inspection and supervision of critical environment-related facility equipment (e.g., controls, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning [HVAC], mechanical systems), building, and grounds regularly for unsafe or abnormal conditions to develop and analyze trends. Understands critical system alarms for multiple discipline(s) of equipment, their meanings, and engages with appropriate escalation processes or procedures. Recognizes circumstances where execution would be considered safe to proceed. Performs various inspections and validations of equipment performance. Monitors the performance from central monitoring locations (i.e., Facility Operations Centers) of maintenance and operations of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) and understands risks or impacts to other subsystems across the data center. Escalates per applicable policies and standards. Utilizes telemetry, control systems, and other platforms to monitor site status, analyze past and current events, as well as other processes, and can identify all alarms. Uses technical expertise, prior experience, and device analytics to recognize trends with equipment behavior and checks potential issues as they arise. Advises less experienced colleagues on issues found while monitoring applicable CE systems. Ensures all monitoring equipment repair, replacement, and maintenance work meets or exceeds Microsoft Service Level Agreement (SLA) requirements. Uses data trends to develop or produce predictive analyses of equipment performance.
Works on complex, advanced tasks (e.g., stabilization, resolution, recovery) independently. Serves as an operations specialist in a major area of operations (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls, generators) and provides oversight and training/mentorship to team members on tasks regarding these subsystems. Demonstrates an understanding of and operates equipment and systems across all disciplines (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls) with knowledge of the interactions between them and overall operation of a data center. Operates all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner.
Safely and quickly responds to and leads an onsite incident response team for all abnormal conditions that impact operations, and coordinates with other critical facilities professionals to perform corrective repairs, without supervision. Gathers necessary information and creates incident timelines/data, root-cause analyses, and/or action items following an abnormal condition as required. Identifies and contacts/engages appropriate parties to mitigate incidents as they occur, and collects or provides appropriate escalation details or context to support incident management requirements. Develops new or follows preexisting emergency operating procedures (EOPs), methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) in relation to incidents. Directly provides and leads and coordinates emergency monitoring response plans for irregular or malfunctioning conditions. Oversees team during emergency incident management, assigning tasks for corrective repair as appropriate. Communicates directly to leadership, advises the business on the current conditions, safety concerns, and next steps for incident mitigation and/or resolution. Oversees incident detection, analysis, and containment efforts. Serves as technical expert in ensuring emergency operating procedures (EOPs) are consistent with proper incident response.
Utilizes internal computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) to track all equipment assets and to complete work order requests for maintenance work. Tracks utilization and time tracking results for team members, within applicable task management systems. Reviews and validates added required data, documents, changes logged, and procedures upkeep details (related to building management systems and reports) conducted by team members. Guides and coaches team in CMMS usage best practices. Audits and reviews team's data to ensure performance adherence to assigned work tasks. Generates reporting from CMMS for outstanding and ongoing work orders. Generates ad hoc or custom CMMS reports as needed for management. Reviews spare equipment and parts, updates stock, and signal stock replenishment with suppliers and/or coordination with Materials Handling partners.
People Management
Managers deliver success through empowerment and accountability by modeling, coaching, and caring. Model: Live our culture. Embody our values. Practice our leadership principles. Coach: Define team objectives and outcomes. Enable success across boundaries. Help the team adapt and learn. Care: Attract and retain great people. Know each individual’s capabilities and aspirations. Invest in the growth of others.

Embody our culture and values

High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent.
5+ years mission critical services work/applied learning experience (e.g., high availability assembly/manufacturing/critical infrastructure environments such as data centers, oil and gas refineries, hospitals, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, or related fields) OR equivalent experience.

Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:
Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.

title: Cybersecurity Infrastructure Engineer - Weekend shift
location: United States, Multiple Locations, Multiple Locations
description:
Overview
With more than 45,000 employees and partners worldwide, the Customer Experience and Success (CE&S) organization is on a mission to empower customers to accelerate business value through differentiated customer experiences that leverage Microsoft products, services and partnerships.
Microsoft's Detection and Response Team (DART) is seeking a skilled and experienced Cybersecurity Infrastructure Engineer to join the team in the United States. DART is the first port of call for many customers during a security incident. This pivotal, customer-facing position helps customers contain, recover from and build resilience against high-impact cybersecurity incidents.
In this role, you will be required to work shift assignments during non-standard business hours, Friday through Monday: 10-hour shift scheduled between 8:00AM - 6PM EDT, Weekends and Public Holidays. Substitute days off will be provided for public holiday work. Working hours may change based on business needs.
You will lead infrastructure recovery and identity containment workstreams, establish technical priorities and act as a trusted technical partner for customers during urgent response activity. Working with lead investigators, threat hunters, reverse engineers and incident coordinators, you will help customers make evidence-led recovery decisions and improve durable security outcomes.
As part of a globally distributed, mission-driven team, you will share practical recovery expertise, mentor colleagues and help shape the future of Defender Experts Cybersecurity Incident Response.
Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. Employees are expected to demonstrate a growth mindset, innovation, collaboration, respect, integrity, accountability and inclusion.
Responsibilities
As a Cybersecurity Infrastructure Engineer, you will lead and support evidence-driven infrastructure response, identity recovery and technical hardening workstreams across enterprise on-premises and cloud environments.
Set infrastructure recovery objectives, technical priorities and evidence requirements for identity, directory, privileged access and enterprise infrastructure workstreams.
Lead or support containment and recovery for compromised Active Directory, Entra ID, Tier 0 and hybrid infrastructure environments.
Assess compromise scope, recovery readiness, trust relationships, privileged access pathways and security-control gaps; establish what is known, what remains uncertain and what additional validation is needed.
Direct or guide technical response activities that balance containment, recovery urgency, evidence preservation and customer business constraints.
Collect, preserve and analyse infrastructure and identity evidence needed to support investigation, containment and recovery decisions.
Serve as a technical point of contact for infrastructure recovery; brief customer technical teams, executives and internal stakeholders with clear findings, priorities and decision options.
Identify skill, access, telemetry and resource gaps early; work with incident coordinators and leadership to resolve dependencies, obtain specialist support and escalate delivery risks.
Maintain technical documentation and clear follow-the-sun handovers covering evidence, decisions, risks, dependencies and next actions; support final reporting and lessons learned.
Contribute to proactive services such as compromise assessments, identity posture reviews and infrastructure resilience improvements.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
Doctorate in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Computer Security, or related field OR Master's Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Computer Security, or related field AND 3+ years experience in software development lifecycle, large-scale computing, threat analysis or modeling, cybersecurity, vulnerability research, and/or anomaly detection
OR Bachelor's Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Computer Security, or related field AND 4+ years experience in software development lifecycle, large-scale computing, threat analysis or modeling, cybersecurity, vulnerability research, and/or anomaly detection
OR equivalent experience.

description:
Overview
We are advancing technological innovation through quantum computing, which has the potential to reshape how complex problems are addressed in science, medicine, materials research, and industry. At Microsoft Quantum, we aim to empower scientists to solve some of the world's biggest problems by developing advanced computing platforms at the intersection of high-performance computing, artificial intelligence, and quantum information technology.
The Microsoft Quantum team is dedicated to developing the first scalable, fault-tolerant quantum computer. Our work spans quantum hardware, error correction, and integration with Azure. Our accomplished, diverse international team is focused on building a scalable quantum computing system. Our full-stack strategy encompasses breakthroughs in quantum device physics, scalable readout, and control infrastructure powered by cryoelectronics. As quantum computing enters a pivotal phase of accelerated growth, this position offers an opportunity to contribute to a transformative technology.
Microsoft is seeking a Quantum Technical Program Manager (TPM), at the Senior to Principal level , to lead the end-to-end delivery of next-generation quantum hardware systems. You will drive cross-functional execution across research, engineering, and external partners to develop scalable, production-ready quantum solutions. Working closely with subsystem research and development leaders in areas such as control, packaging, and test and measurement, you will align roadmaps, manage risks, and deliver critical milestones. This high-impact leadership role calls for deep technical expertise, strong program management skills, and a customer-focused mindset.
You will collaborate with physicists, quantum theorists, experimentalists, research and systems engineers, technical program managers, supply chain experts, cloud architects, and external partners to accelerate the scale-up of topological qubits and quantum systems. If you thrive on complex program challenges, can navigate ambiguity, and are passionate about foundational technologies, we invite you to help shape the future of quantum computing.
At Microsoft, our mission—to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more—guides how we partner with customers to deliver trusted, impactful solutions. With a growth mindset culture, we innovate responsibly and measure success by shared progress—people, teams, and customers. Join us to do meaningful work that changes the world and helps shape what’s next for everyone.

Collaborate with system architects, research scientists, and hardware engineers to achieve program goals.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting up to 25lbs / 11kg without assistance. Occasional lifting 25-50lbs / 11-22.5kg with lift assistance. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
May conduct, assists in conducting, and/or participates in daily safety briefings. Traveling up to 25% typically domestically to and from multiple locations during the workday, and occasionally domestically to other sites for overnight stays. May work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.
Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.
Managing Service Maintains an awareness of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) through reporting dashboards, systems, for personal monthly performance discussions as needed.
Escalates and/or seeks guidance from experienced technicians or direct-line management regarding client interactions.
Completes required training aligned to job focus areas and workloads (i.e., Break fix, Deployment, Simple Change, Decommission, IT Critical Environment) in a timely manner per direct-line management assignment(s). Actively mentors and supports training of other technicians through on-the-job training (OJT) and by providing direct guidance on specific job focus areas and workloads (i.e., Break fix, Deployment, Simple Change, Decommission, IT Critical Environment). May complete additional or supplemental training to obtain or maintain relevant industry or technical certifications.
Develops a comprehensive understanding of cross-functional Data Center processes to support partnerships with internal and external stakeholders.

Prepares, stages, sets up, and performs basic startups and shutdowns for hardware (e.g., racks, hard drives, switches) according to specific written instructions provided via checklists, guides, standard processes, emails, while providing guidance to less experienced technicians, with direction from management where applicable. May perform tasks in tandem with other technicians to comply with procedures and safety requirements.
Applies advanced diagnostics and troubleshooting expertise and/or leverages standard procedures to quickly and efficiently identify the cause(s) of technical issues and replace faulty components in network, storage, or server equipment with zero-to-minimal customer and/or business disruption. Maintains advanced awareness of conditions, circumstances, and scenarios which may reflect significant customer or business impact within the Data Center environment, and escalates observations of imminent incident risks or potential situations immediately to direct-line management.
Performs discrete quality control activities and assessment of work, to compliance standards and process adherence, performed by other technicians. Regularly performs post-execution verification of grounding, staging, labeling, and cabling to align with all safety protocols, deployment standards, and planned Network Design Templates (NDTs). Identifies errors in deployment standards or Network Design Templates (NDTs) and escalates to relevant technicians, specialists, or internal business partners to coordinate corrections as needed.
Follows procedures to immediately communicate, report, and escalate data center technical or safety related incidents to direct-line management. Participates in bridge calls to provide details on incident status and executes on-site follow-up actions as directed if necessary. May leverage learnings to contribute to the improvement of quality of service and support.
Directly performs decommissions, simple changes (e.g., memory upgrades, OS rebuilds) complex changes (e.g. upgrading entire racks) and refreshes of infrastructure cabling, network, storage, and server equipment, following standard procedures with minimal-to-no guidance. We are seeking a BIM Designer & Coordinator to support the planning and design of large-scale industrial and mission-critical facilities. In this role, you will develop, coordinate, and maintain multidisciplinary BIM models across Civil, Electrical, Mechanical, Architectural, and Structural disciplines, enabling early design validation, constructability reviews, equipment planning, and cross-functional coordination.

 - Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, equipment layouts, design narratives, diagrams, and consultant deliverables.
